AI.motivation: To reconstruct high-fidelity, freely navigable 3D scenes from a single 360° panorama without per-scene optimization or multi-view capture, addressing limitations of existing methods that lack metric trajectory control or struggle with large disocclusions under long-range camera motion.
AI.method: Two-stage feed-forward pipeline: (1) A NavMesh-planned SE(3) roaming trajectory is injected into a latent video diffusion model via dense geometry-warped conditioning, with long-short trajectory mixed training and a self-consistency objective based on shortcut models to produce high-fidelity video in four CFG-free denoising steps. (2) A feed-forward panoramic reconstructor lifts the generated video into a 3D Gaussian scene.
AI.result: Outperforms geometry-conditioned baselines in both panoramic video generation and downstream 3D reconstruction, while generalizing zero-shot to unseen indoor scenes.
AI.conclusion: The generated 3D scene supports real-time, free-viewpoint roaming and can be directly used as a simulation-ready asset for embodied AI applications.

title: AIGen: Automating AI Bill of Materials Generation Through Hybrid MLOps Integration
summary: The responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) systems requires rigorous documentation of their constituent artifacts, e.g., datasets, model weights, training pipelines, and runtime dependencies. Although the Software Package Data Exchange (SPDX) 3.0 standard introduced native support for AI and dataset profiles, practical tooling capable of generating standards-compliant AI Bills of Materials (AIBoMs) in an automated and extensible manner remains scarce. This paper presents AIGen, a modular AIBoM generator that produces machine-readable, interoperable inventories of AI system components that comply with the SPDX 3.0 AI profile. AIGen works on top of the MLflow MLOps framework and combines mining heuristics with Large Language Models to generate AIBoMs. A plugin interface allows practitioners to extend the tool with domain-specific collectors without modifying the core codebase, supporting heterogeneous AI frameworks such as Hugging Face, PyTorch, and TensorFlow. AIGen is designed to facilitate compliance with the European Union AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001, providing a concrete, reusable foundation for transparent, accountable AI supply chain governance. Tool URL: https://github.com/danielebifolco/AIGen Tool Video: https://youtu.be/\_nAbXDWfVL4

AI.tldr: AIGen is a modular, automated tool for generating SPDX 3.0-compliant AI Bills of Materials (AIBoMs) by integrating with MLflow, using heuristics and LLMs, and supporting extensible plugins for diverse AI frameworks to enhance AI supply chain transparency and regulatory compliance.
AI.motivation: Responsible AI development requires rigorous documentation of AI artifacts (datasets, models, pipelines), but practical, automated tooling for generating standards-compliant AIBoMs is scarce despite the SPDX 3.0 standard introducing native AI support.
AI.method: AIGen is built on top of MLflow MLOps framework, combining mining heuristics with Large Language Models to generate AIBoMs. It provides a plugin interface for domain-specific collectors without modifying core code, supporting Hugging Face, PyTorch, and TensorFlow.
AI.result: AIGen produces machine-readable, interoperable, SPDX 3.0 AI profile-compliant inventories of AI system components in an automated and extensible manner.
AI.conclusion: AIGen facilitates compliance with the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001, providing a reusable foundation for transparent, accountable AI supply chain governance.

title: Anchoring and Steering Diffusion: Enhancing the Faithfulness of Text-to-Image Generation at Inference Time
summary: While text-to-image diffusion models achieve impressive visual quality, they frequently struggle to maintain precise alignment with complex compositional prompts. An effective strategy is to improve the inference process of diffusion models, thereby better leveraging their pretrained priors to address misalignment. Existing training-free methods can be divided into two categories. The first category focuses on improving the randomly sampled initial noise, either performing costly search over noise pools or manipulating sampled noise without ensuring reliable semantic injection. The second category focuses on improving the denoising trajectory, lacking explicit mechanisms to timely diagnose and correct semantic errors. we propose \textbf{AnchorSteer}, a training-free framework that exerts fine-grained control over \textbf{both initialization} and \textbf{the denoising trajectory}. AnchorSteer consists of two synergistic components: \textbf{Semantic Anchoring} replaces uninformative Gaussian noise with text-aligned initializations via CLIP-based prior extraction and a novel Latent-Prior Score Distillation Sampling (LP-SDS) objective. Specifically, LP-SDS distills CLIP visual priors into the knowledge distribution of diffusion models, mitigating the domain gap between CLIP-based priors and diffusion-based priors. \textbf{Reflective Steering} transforms passive denoising with an active Think--Erase--Retouch loop that enables mid-generation self-correction. It leverages VLM-based diagnosis to detect semantic deviations and performs targeted latent refinement to suppress erroneous content and recover missing attributes. Extensive experiments on GenEval and T2I-CompBench++ demonstrate that AnchorSteer consistently outperforms existing baselines in text--image alignment while preserving high visual quality.

AI.tldr: AnchorSteer is a training-free framework that improves text-to-image alignment in diffusion models by jointly optimizing both initial noise (via Semantic Anchoring with LP-SDS) and denoising trajectory (via Reflective Steering with Think-Erase-Retouch self-correction), outperforming existing methods on GenEval and T2I-CompBench++.
AI.motivation: Text-to-image diffusion models struggle with precise alignment to complex compositional prompts; existing training-free methods either focus only on initial noise optimization (costly search or unreliable injection) or denoising trajectory improvement (lacking timely diagnosis/correction), but neither achieves fine-grained control over both aspects.
AI.method: AnchorSteer has two synergistic components: (1) Semantic Anchoring replaces random Gaussian noise with text-aligned initializations via CLIP-based prior extraction and a novel LP-SDS objective that distills CLIP visual priors into diffusion knowledge distribution, bridging the domain gap; (2) Reflective Steering transforms passive denoising with an active Think-Erase-Retouch loop using VLM-based diagnosis to detect semantic deviations and perform targeted latent refinement to suppress errors and recover attributes.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on GenEval and T2I-CompBench++ demonstrate that AnchorSteer consistently outperforms existing baselines in text-image alignment while preserving high visual quality.
AI.conclusion: Jointly controlling both initialization and denoising trajectory in a training-free manner yields superior compositional alignment for diffusion models.

title: Efficient Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization for Risk-Aware AutoRL
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown remarkable success across a wide range of complex tasks. However, RL outcomes can be highly stochastic, and both expected performance and variability often depend on hyperparameter (HP) configurations. We propose efficient and risk-averse heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization (ERAHBO), a Bayesian optimization method that models both the mean and variance of learning outcomes as functions of the HP configurations. ERAHBO aims to identify HP configurations that achieve high average return while reducing variability across training runs, and it improves the sample efficiency of the HP optimization via adaptive re-sampling rather than a fixed budget per HP. Empirical evaluations across diverse RL algorithms and environments demonstrate that ERAHBO generally outperforms both risk-neutral and risk-averse baselines, delivering improved sample efficiency for risk-averse returns.

AI.tldr: ERAHBO is a Bayesian optimization method for hyperparameter tuning in reinforcement learning that models both mean and variance of returns, identifying configurations that achieve high average return with low variability while improving sample efficiency through adaptive re-sampling.
AI.motivation: RL outcomes are highly stochastic and sensitive to hyperparameter configurations; existing methods often ignore the variability (risk) across training runs or use inefficient fixed budgets per HP.
AI.method: Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization that jointly models mean and variance of learning outcomes as functions of HP configurations, employing adaptive re-sampling instead of a fixed budget per HP to improve sample efficiency.
AI.result: ERAHBO generally outperforms both risk-neutral and risk-averse baselines across diverse RL algorithms and environments, delivering improved sample efficiency for risk-averse returns.
AI.conclusion: ERAHBO effectively balances high average performance with low variability in RL hyperparameter optimization, offering a sample-efficient risk-averse solution.

title: Physically Real-time Infrared Attack against Optical Flow Estimation Networks
summary: With the promising performance of deep neural networks on image-based tasks, different real-world applications such as autonomous driving and motion detection have become increasingly mature and relevant to human lives. In particular, Optical Flow Estimation Networks (OFENs), as upstream models, play a critical role in different domains. Its outputs are heavily assumed and adopted for different downstream tasks, and it is essential to test its robustness to prevent safety accidents. We present an approach for real-time attacks on OFENs in the physical world, leveraging infrared lights for their stealthiness. By generating a large number of Adversarial Examples in advance, our approach computes AEs in real time and dynamically displays them, which allows our method to facilitate precise and targeted attacks without modifying the victim system. Unlike previous digital-to-physical attack techniques, our method directly attacks victim models within the physical world, thereby overcoming the limitations associated with the ineffectiveness of AEs. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in compromising OFENs across diverse lighting conditions, varying object motion velocities, and different object placements, ultimately impairing the network's ability to accurately estimate optical flow.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a real-time physical-world attack on Optical Flow Estimation Networks (OFENs) using infrared lights to generate adversarial examples dynamically, successfully compromising the models across varying conditions without modifying victim systems.
AI.motivation: OFENs are critical upstream models for downstream tasks like autonomous driving and motion detection, and their robustness must be tested to prevent safety accidents caused by unreliable optical flow estimates.
AI.method: The approach pre-generates a large number of Adversarial Examples (AEs) and computes them in real-time, dynamically displaying them via infrared lights for stealth. This enables direct physical-world attacks on victim models without modifying the system, overcoming limitations of prior digital-to-physical attack techniques.
AI.result: Experimental results show the method effectively compromises OFENs across diverse lighting conditions, varying object motion velocities, and different object placements, significantly impairing the network's optical flow estimation accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The proposed infrared-based real-time physical attack successfully demonstrates that OFENs are vulnerable to stealthy adversarial perturbations in the physical world, highlighting critical safety concerns for real-world applications.

title: Universality and Approximation Rates of Graph Neural Networks with Random Features
summary: We investigate message-passing graph neural networks with random node features. Random node features are known to enhance the expressiveness of graph neural networks (GNNs) both theoretically and empirically. Here, we establish a novel universality result focusing on permutation-equivariant neural networks (PENNs), a class of GNNs built from feedforward neural network components that subsumes many prominent GNN architectures. We show that PENNs, combined with partially random node features, can approximate arbitrarily well in probability any measurable permutation-invariant or permutation-equivariant function on directed graphs of fixed size with multidimensional node and edge features. For $k$-times continuously differentiable functions, $k\geq 2$, we also derive upper bounds on the approximation rates, relating the complexity of the feedforward components of a PENN in terms of layer depth and number of nonzero weights to the desired approximation accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that permutation-equivariant neural networks (PENNs) with random node features can universally approximate any permutation-invariant/equivariant function on fixed-size directed graphs, with convergence rates for smooth functions.
AI.motivation: To establish a novel universality result for GNNs using random node features, extending theoretical understanding of their expressiveness beyond existing results.
AI.method: The authors analyze PENNs (a GNN class built from feedforward networks) combined with partially random node features, proving they can approximate any measurable permutation-invariant/equivariant function on fixed-size directed graphs with multidimensional node and edge features. They also derive approximation rate bounds for $k$-times continuously differentiable functions ($k\geq 2$).
AI.result: PENNs with random node features achieve universal approximation in probability for permutation-invariant/equivariant functions on fixed-size directed graphs, with explicit upper bounds on approximation rates relating network complexity (layer depth and number of nonzero weights) to approximation accuracy for smooth functions.
AI.conclusion: Random node features significantly enhance GNN expressiveness theoretically, enabling universal approximation with convergence guarantees; this provides a theoretical foundation for their empirical success.

title: Visko Orbis 1.0: A Live Model for Real-Time Interactive Long Video Generation
summary: We present Visko Orbis 1.0, a Live Model for real-time, interactive long-video generation. Users can change the prompt at any moment during generation, and the update becomes visible in real time. Visko Orbis 1.0 supports long-form text-to-video, image-to-video, and video continuation, with multilingual prompts and prompt switching while generation is in progress. A bounded multi-scale memory preserves subjects, scenes, and style across chunks, sustaining hour-scale rollouts without evident quality or color drift. Built on a distilled chunk-wise streaming generator and a streaming video upscaler, Visko Orbis 1.0 delivers real-time 4K video generation at 24 FPS using an optimized GPU serving engine. In long-form Arena comparisons, Visko Orbis 1.0 obtains the highest overall-preference and temporal-stability ratings among state-of-the-art real-time interactive video-generation systems.

AI.tldr: Visko Orbis 1.0 is a live model for real-time, interactive long-video generation supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, and video continuation with multilingual prompts, bounded multi-scale memory, and real-time 4K output at 24 FPS, achieving top preference and temporal-stability ratings in long-form Arena comparisons.
AI.motivation: To enable real-time, interactive long-video generation where users can dynamically change prompts during generation with immediate visible updates, overcoming limitations of prior non-interactive or short-duration video generation systems.
AI.method: A distilled chunk-wise streaming generator combined with a streaming video upscaler, a bounded multi-scale memory mechanism for preserving subjects/scenes/style across chunks, and an optimized GPU serving engine for real-time 4K output at 24 FPS.
AI.result: Achieves the highest overall-preference and temporal-stability ratings among state-of-the-art real-time interactive video-generation systems in long-form Arena comparisons.
AI.conclusion: Visko Orbis 1.0 demonstrates real-time, interactive long-video generation with sustained hour-scale rollouts, multilingual prompt support, and no evident quality or color drift, establishing a new standard for live video generation systems.

title: Mixture-of-experts for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors
summary: The use of digital pens for online handwriting trajectory reconstruction is a prevalent method for human-computer interaction. In this study, we focus on a digital pen equipped with sensors where we aim at reconstructing the online handwriting trajectory. This pen enables writing on any surface and preserving the digital trace of handwriting. This type of pen could be used as an aid to learning to write in classroom. In this paper, we propose a new approach learning to finely reconstruct the touching trajectories while precisely analyzing the hovering part in order to position the next touching trace correctly. This relies on a Mixture-Of-Experts (MOE) approach. The first expert is dedicated for the pencil touch, and is named touching expert model. The second one is dedicated for the hovering pen trajectory, and is named hovering expert model. We improve on the learning of each of these experts based on additional context or specific examples. In addition we introduce a novel public benchmark dataset, to enable future research and comparisons in the field of handwriting reconstruction. The results demonstrates a significant enhancement compared to its primary competitors.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Mixture-Of-Experts (MOE) approach for reconstructing online handwriting trajectories from a digital pen, with separate expert models for touching and hovering phases, and introduces a new public benchmark dataset.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate handwriting trajectory reconstruction from a digital pen that can write on any surface, particularly as an aid for learning to write in classroom settings, while addressing the challenge of correctly positioning the next touching trace by analyzing the hovering trajectory.
AI.method: A Mixture-Of-Experts (MOE) approach with two experts: a touching expert model for pencil touch trajectory reconstruction and a hovering expert model for hovering pen trajectory analysis. Each expert is improved through additional context and specific examples.
AI.result: The proposed approach demonstrates significant enhancement compared to its primary competitors. A novel public benchmark dataset is also introduced to facilitate future research.
AI.conclusion: The MOE-based approach with separate experts for touching and hovering phases effectively improves online handwriting reconstruction, and the new benchmark dataset will support further advancements in the field.

title: Sequence-SOD: Bio-inspired Sequence-aware Spiking ObjectDetection for Event Cameras
summary: Event cameras follow a retina-inspired sensing principle, reporting local intensity changes asynchronously with hightemporal resolution and a wide dynamic range. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) complement these sparse event streams through brain-inspired dynamics, using sparse spikes and leaky membrane potentials to integrate information over time. However, many SNN object detectors process isolated event intervals with a single label and reset the network state after each prediction, thereby underusing temporal information in continuous event streams. We introduce Sequence-SOD, a sequence-aware SNN object detector that processes extended event sequences containing labels at multiple time points. Events are accumulated into short intervals, discretized into temporal steps, and fed sequentially to an SSD-style Spiking DenseNet while preserving membrane potentials across intervals within a sequence, so that detection is driven by an evolving neural state instead of independently reset input windows. On the Gen1 Automotive Detection Dataset, sequence-aware training improves mAP from 23.38 for single-interval training to 25.30 without augmentation and to 26.88 withevent-data augmentation. The model achieves a theoretical prediction frequency of 40 Hz. Training and evaluating SNN object detectors on extended event sequences improves their ability to exploit temporal cues while preserving the energy-efficiency benefits of sparse spiking computation. The results highlight sequence-aware training as a complementary direction to architectural improvements for event-based SNN detection.

AI.tldr: Sequence-SOD is a sequence-aware SNN object detector that processes extended event sequences with multi-label temporal windows. By maintaining membrane potentials across intervals instead of resetting per prediction, it improves mAP from 23.38 to 25.30 (and 26.88 with augmentation) on Gen1 dataset at 40 Hz, demonstrating that sequence-aware training enhances temporal cue exploitation in event-based SNN detection.
AI.motivation: Current SNN object detectors process isolated event intervals with single labels and reset network state after each prediction, underutilizing temporal information in continuous event streams. The paper aims to enable SNN detectors to leverage extended temporal sequences with multiple labels by maintaining evolving neural states across intervals.
AI.method: Events are accumulated into short intervals, discretized into temporal steps, and fed sequentially to an SSD-style Spiking DenseNet. Crucially, membrane potentials are preserved across intervals within a sequence rather than being reset, allowing the neural state to evolve across time and drive detection from a temporally integrated representation.
AI.result: On Gen1 dataset: sequence-aware training improves mAP from 23.38 (single-interval) to 25.30 (no augmentation) and 26.88 (with event-data augmentation). The model achieves 40 Hz theoretical prediction frequency.
AI.conclusion: Sequence-aware training improves SNN object detectors' ability to exploit temporal cues while maintaining energy-efficient sparse spiking computation. This is a complementary direction to architectural improvements for event-based SNN detection.

title: PowerAtlas: Towards Electricity-Computing Co-Scheduling for Power Systems
summary: The rapid growth of AI workloads is turning data centers into large-scale, volatile, yet spatiotemporally flexible grid loads, creating an urgent need for coordinated electricity-computing scheduling. Under stringent grid constraints, schedules from general-purpose large language models (LLMs) are often infeasible, causing line-flow violations and unserved load. We present PowerAtlas, an LLM-agent framework for electricity-computing co-scheduling that integrates historical instances, domain knowledge, and physical constraints to produce joint decisions satisfying both grid operational rules and the service-level agreements (SLAs) of computing tasks. Working with a provincial power utility in China, we built an experimental electricity-computing network and validated the decision loop on real data-center data; from de-identified operational data we further constructed ECBench, a benchmark of 2,000 scheduling instances with oracle-optimal solutions. Experiments across eleven LLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of PowerAtlas under realistic physical operating conditions, with consistent feasibility and cost gains across three open-weight backbones. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/JAVA-Jiang/PowerAtlas.

AI.tldr: PowerAtlas is an LLM-agent framework for coordinated electricity-computing scheduling in AI data centers that integrates domain knowledge and physical constraints to produce feasible joint decisions, validated with a provincial utility in China on the ECBench benchmark of 2,000 instances.
AI.motivation: The rapid growth of AI workloads is turning data centers into large-scale, volatile grid loads, and general-purpose LLMs often produce infeasible schedules that violate grid constraints, creating an urgent need for coordinated electricity-computing co-scheduling.
AI.method: PowerAtlas is an LLM-agent framework integrating historical instances, domain knowledge, and physical constraints to produce joint scheduling decisions satisfying both grid operational rules and computing task SLAs; validated on a real experimental electricity-computing network with a provincial utility in China, and benchmarked via ECBench (2,000 scheduling instances with oracle-optimal solutions).
AI.result: Across eleven LLMs, PowerAtlas demonstrates consistent feasibility and cost gains under realistic physical operating conditions across three open-weight backbones.
AI.conclusion: PowerAtlas effectively enables feasible, physically constrained electricity-computing co-scheduling for AI data centers, outperforming general-purpose LLMs in both grid compliance and cost efficiency.

title: TPD: Temporal Prior Decoupling for Text-to-Video Diffusion Models
summary: Text-to-video diffusion models generate temporally coherent content from natural language, yet when a prompt describes an early scene that persists while a new event emerges on top of it---such as "a tall sandcastle standing on a beach where a wave rushes in and washes it away"---generation frequently fails to realize the late-segment event in the corresponding frames. We identify this failure as Temporal Prior Suppression (TPS): the dominant prior of the early segment captures the cross-attention trajectory across the temporal axis and suppresses the guidance signal needed for late-segment realization, a competing tendency existing guidance mechanisms do not model. We introduce Temporal Prior Decoupling (TPD), a training-free framework that restores suppressed late-segment signals during diffusion sampling. TPD constructs a temporal counterfactual by conditioning on the early segment alone, and defines the discrepancy between the full-prompt and counterfactual trajectories as a suppressed signal direction. Rather than removing this direction as in prior subtractive projection methods, TPD restores it through a frame-selective lower-bound constraint resolved jointly over diffusion timestep and video frame, realizing the suppressed event in the late frames without disrupting early-segment coherence: where prior work enforces upper-bound feasibility to remove unwanted semantics, TPD enforces lower-bound feasibility to guarantee suppressed-signal contribution. TPD runs entirely within standard diffusion sampling without retraining, and is defined purely in classifier-free guidance space, making it backbone-agnostic by construction. Experiments show that TPD significantly improves late-concept realization while preserving temporal coherence and visual fidelity, and that the targeted suppression recurs across distinct text-to-video backbones.

AI.tldr: TPD is a training-free framework that restores suppressed late-segment signals in text-to-video diffusion models by constructing temporal counterfactuals and enforcing lower-bound feasibility, solving the Temporal Prior Suppression problem.
AI.motivation: Text-to-video diffusion models fail to generate late-segment events when an early scene persists and a new event emerges on top of it (e.g., a sandcastle being washed away by a wave). This failure, termed Temporal Prior Suppression (TPS), occurs because the dominant early-segment prior suppresses the guidance signal needed for late-segment realization—a competing tendency existing guidance mechanisms do not model.
AI.method: Temporal Prior Decoupling (TPD) constructs a temporal counterfactual by conditioning only on the early segment, defines the discrepancy between full-prompt and counterfactual trajectories as the suppressed signal direction, and restores it via a frame-selective lower-bound constraint resolved jointly over diffusion timestep and video frame. Unlike prior subtractive projection methods that enforce upper-bound feasibility to remove unwanted semantics, TPD enforces lower-bound feasibility to guarantee suppressed-signal contribution. It operates purely in classifier-free guidance space without retraining.
AI.result: TPD significantly improves late-concept realization while preserving temporal coherence and visual fidelity. The targeted suppression (TPS) is shown to recur across distinct text-to-video backbones.
AI.conclusion: TPD effectively addresses Temporal Prior Suppression in text-to-video diffusion models through a training-free, backbone-agnostic framework that restores suppressed late-segment signals via lower-bound constraint optimization, outperforming prior methods.

title: Domain adaptation for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors
summary: Digital pens are commonly used to write on digital devices, providing the handwriting trace and enhancing human-computer interation. This study focuses on a digital pen equipped with kinematic sensors, allowing users to write on any surface while simultaneously preserving a digital trajectory of handwriting. This technology holds significant potential as a valuable educational tool, particularly in classrooms where it can facilitate the process of learning to write. A major issue is based on the difference in captured signals between adults and children. For similar handwriting trace, we have large differences in sensor signals due to differences in speed and confidence in the handwriting gesture of children. To address this, we investigate a domain adaptation approach to build a unified intermediate feature representation aimed at facilitating the trajectory reconstruction. We demonstrate the interest of domain adaptation methods in leveraging existing knowledge for application in different contexts. Specifically, we compare our domain adaptation approach with two other methods: training the model from scratch and fine-tuning the model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a domain adaptation approach for reconstructing handwriting trajectories from a kinematic sensor-equipped digital pen. The key challenge is the signal difference between adults and children due to variations in writing speed and confidence. The authors build a unified intermediate feature representation to enable trajectory reconstruction across age groups, and compare this method against training from scratch and fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Digital pens with kinematic sensors enable handwriting on any surface while preserving digital trajectories. However, significant signal differences between adults and children (due to varying speed and confidence) pose a major challenge for handwriting trajectory reconstruction, motivating the need for a domain adaptation solution.
AI.method: The authors investigate a domain adaptation approach to build a unified intermediate feature representation that facilitates trajectory reconstruction across different age groups. They compare their domain adaptation method against two baselines: training the model from scratch and fine-tuning an existing model.
AI.result: The domain adaptation approach demonstrates effectiveness in leveraging existing knowledge for trajectory reconstruction in different contexts (adults vs. children), showing advantages over training from scratch and fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Domain adaptation is a promising strategy for handling cross-population variability in sensor-based handwriting reconstruction, enabling more robust digital pen systems as educational tools for diverse age groups.

title: FreeShadow: Training-Free Shadow Removal via Illumination Transfer and Selective Content Preservation in Diffusion Models
summary: Existing supervised and unsupervised shadow removal methods often suffer from limited generalization due to the insufficient diversity of available training datasets, while zero-shot methods tend to produce artifacts and require time-consuming test-time optimization. To address these issues, we propose FreeShadow, a training-free shadow removal method built upon pretrained diffusion models, which exploits diffusion priors for shadow removal without any training or optimization. For illumination recovery, we propose an illumination transfer attention (ITA), which re-weights the self-attention maps in diffusion model to transfer illumination cues from non-shadow to shadow regions. For content preservation, we analyze the effects of illumination variations on self-attention maps and latent high-frequency features in diffusion model, and selectively preserve illumination-invariant components to maintain content fidelity while suppressing residual shadows. We further propose local texture-preserving relighting (LTPR) to mitigate local texture misalignment caused by VAE compression. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves strong generalization and produces realistic shadow-free images.

AI.tldr: FreeShadow is a training-free shadow removal method using pretrained diffusion models, leveraging illumination transfer attention and content preservation techniques to remove shadows without training or optimization, achieving strong generalization and realistic results.
AI.motivation: Existing supervised/unsupervised shadow removal methods suffer from limited generalization due to insufficient training data diversity, while zero-shot methods produce artifacts and require time-consuming test-time optimization.
AI.method: FreeShadow uses a pretrained diffusion model with three key components: (1) Illumination Transfer Attention (ITA) re-weights self-attention maps to transfer illumination cues from non-shadow to shadow regions; (2) Content preservation by analyzing illumination variations on self-attention maps and latent high-frequency features, selectively preserving illumination-invariant components; (3) Local Texture-Preserving Relighting (LTPR) to mitigate local texture misalignment from VAE compression.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate strong generalization and realistic shadow-free image generation.
AI.conclusion: FreeShadow achieves training-free, optimization-free shadow removal with strong generalization, addressing limitations of supervised, unsupervised, and zero-shot methods.

title: CalTwin: Towards Calibrated, Shift-Robust Medical World Models via Fisher-Information Regularisation
summary: Medical world models aim to learn a latent state of patient or organ physiology and a transition function that forecasts how that state evolves under interventions, supporting downstream tasks from imaging-based diagnosis to digital-twin treatment planning. Two failure modes threaten the reliability of such models in clinical deployment: (i)~\emph{covariate shift}, because training data are fragmented across hospitals, scanners, and time, so the feature distribution seen by the latent-dynamics predictor differs across fragments and from the distribution at deployment; and (ii)~\emph{confidence misalignment}, because multi-step forecasts are often overconfident exactly where clinical risk is highest. We argue that both problems admit a unified treatment via a single lightweight regularisation objective, \textbf{CalTwin}, which combines a Fisher-Information-based shift penalty adapted from our prior work on fragmented covariate-shift remediation~\cite{khan2025mitigating,khan2025causal} with a Confidence Misalignment Penalty adapted from our prior work on calibrated vision-language classification~\cite{khan2025confidence}, applied here to a GRU-based medical world model's latent transition predictor. We derive the combined objective, establish which proof steps transfer from the classification setting without modification and which require adaptation, and evaluate it on the PhysioNet 2019 Sepsis Challenge, treating the two hospital systems as sequential training fragments and the unseen system as an out-of-distribution test. CalTwin reduces OOD next-step latent-state MSE by 9.1\% relative to the no-penalty baseline (FIM penalty alone accounts for 7.0\%); the ECE reduction from the Confidence Misalignment Penalty is real but small (0.7\% for CalTwin, 1.3\% for CMP alone).

AI.tldr: The paper introduces CalTwin, a unified regularisation objective combining a Fisher-Information-based covariate-shift penalty and a confidence misalignment penalty to improve the reliability of medical world models (GRU-based) under distribution shift and overconfidence, with evaluation on the PhysioNet 2019 Sepsis Challenge showing a 9.1% reduction in OOD next-step MSE and small ECE improvement.
AI.motivation: Medical world models suffer from two key failure modes in clinical deployment: covariate shift (training data fragmented across hospitals/scanners/time) and confidence misalignment (multi-step forecasts are overconfident where clinical risk is highest). Both problems threaten reliability and require a unified solution.
AI.method: CalTwin combines a Fisher-Information-based shift penalty (for fragmented covariate-shift remediation) with a Confidence Misalignment Penalty (for calibrated classification) applied to a GRU-based medical world model's latent transition predictor. The combined objective is derived, with identification of which proof steps transfer from classification and which require adaptation.
AI.result: On PhysioNet 2019 Sepsis Challenge (two hospital systems as training fragments, unseen system as OOD test): CalTwin reduces OOD next-step latent-state MSE by 9.1% vs no-penalty baseline (FIM penalty alone: 7.0%); ECE reduction from CMP is small (0.7% for CalTwin, 1.3% for CMP alone).
AI.conclusion: CalTwin provides a unified lightweight regularisation that addresses both covariate shift and confidence misalignment in medical world models, with primary gains from the shift penalty and modest calibration improvements from the confidence penalty.

title: CASIAL: Geometric Distortion Robust Image Watermarking
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 6 tables. Supplementary material included
summary: Deep learning-based watermarking has shown strong robustness against non-geometric distortions, yet its performance under geometric transformations remains limited. Such transformations induce two fundamental failure modes: region removal, such as cropping or masking, which eliminates the information carried by removed pixels, and desynchronization, such as scaling or rotation, which misaligns pixel positions and disrupts decoding. We argue that achieving geometric robustness requires two essential properties: (1) global spread of the watermark message, ensuring resilience even when large regions are removed, and (2) geometry-invariant representations, enabling decoding to remain synchronized despite spatial transformations. Building on these insights, we propose CASIAL, a geometric distortion-robust watermarking framework with cover image-aware message spreading (CAS) strategy and invariance alignment learning (IAL) module. CAS tightly couples watermark bits with cover image features and distributes them adaptively across the entire image, enhancing per-pixel information capacity and robustness to region removal. IAL leverages spatial attention to capture cross-pixel dependencies and align perturbed features into a shared geometry-invariant representation space, mitigating failures due to desynchronization. Across six challenging geometric transformations, CASIAL achieves substantially stronger robustness than eleven prior baselines while preserving high visual quality. It also maintains competitive performance under six signal distortions and four photometric transformations. Notably, although trained only with white-box distortions, CASIAL also exhibits strong transfer robustness to unseen black-box distortions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the broad robustness and superior visual quality of our method.

AI.tldr: CASIAL is a deep watermarking framework that achieves geometric distortion robustness through cover image-aware adaptive message spreading (CAS) and geometry-invariant representation alignment (IAL), significantly outperforming prior methods across diverse geometric, signal, and photometric distortions.
AI.motivation: Deep learning-based watermarking is robust to non-geometric distortions but vulnerable to geometric transformations (region removal like cropping/masking and desynchronization like scaling/rotation). The authors argue that geometric robustness requires global spread of watermark message and geometry-invariant representations, which existing methods lack.
AI.method: Proposes CASIAL framework with two key modules: (1) CAS (Cover image-Aware message Spreading) — tightly couples watermark bits with cover image features and distributes them adaptively across the entire image to enhance per-pixel information capacity and robustness to region removal. (2) IAL (Invariance Alignment Learning) — uses spatial attention to capture cross-pixel dependencies and aligns perturbed features into a shared geometry-invariant representation space, mitigating desynchronization failures.
AI.result: CASIAL substantially outperforms eleven prior baselines across six challenging geometric transformations, maintains competitive performance under six signal distortions and four photometric transformations, preserves high visual quality, and shows strong transfer robustness to unseen black-box distortions despite being trained only with white-box distortions.
AI.conclusion: CASIAL achieves superior robustness to geometric transformations (region removal and desynchronization) via cover image-aware message spreading (CAS) and invariance alignment learning (IAL), outperforming eleven baselines across six geometric distortions while maintaining high visual quality and transfer robustness to unseen black-box distortions.

title: Journey Operators for Structured Multi-Axis Composition
summary:
Many kinds of data have structure along one or more axes: words in a sentence, pixels in an image, nodes in a tree, frames in audio, or cells in a 3D volume. Along one axis, order matters: "the dog bit the man" is different from "the man bit the dog." Across independent axes, however, neither composition nor movement should depend on the order of axes: in an image, composing right then down should give the same result as composing down then right, and moving right then down should describe the same relative position as moving down then right.
  We develop a framework for modeling this kind of multi-axis structure. Each data item carries its content together with a small transformation for each axis. A path connecting two positions defines a journey; the journey operator is the product of per-axis transformations along that path, governing both how data composes along the path and how relative position is described. When the transformations are fixed, our framework recovers Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) and its multi-dimensional variants. When they depend on the data, the model gains a content-adaptive positional inductive bias.
  We show exactly when these paths are well-defined: both composition and movement across axes are path-independent precisely when the axis transformations commute. We also prove that, under the stated toral-frame symmetry, cocycle, bilinearity, and norm-preservation assumptions, the resulting pairwise scoring rule must take the form of block-wise rotations, explaining why RoPE-like methods arise naturally.
  Finally, we use this theory to design JoFormer, a model for value aggregation, and relate it to attention and state-space models (SSMs).
  Initial experiments across vision, language, and length generalization suggest that these inductive biases can have observable consequences in
  practice.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a mathematical framework for modeling data with multiple structured axes (e.g., images, sentences, audio) using per-axis transformations. It shows that when axis transformations commute, composition and movement become path-independent, and under symmetry constraints, the scoring rule reduces to block-wise rotations—explaining why RoPE-like methods emerge naturally. The framework is used to design JoFormer, a model for value aggregation linking attention and SSMs, with experiments showing practical benefits across vision, language, and length generalization.
AI.motivation: Data often has structure along multiple axes (e.g., pixels in an image, words in a sentence). While order matters within an axis, operations across independent axes should be commutative (e.g., composing right then down equals down then right). Existing positional encoding methods like RoPE handle per-axis structure but are fixed; this work seeks a principled framework to capture multi-axis structure with content-adaptive inductive biases.
AI.method: The authors formalize each data item with content and per-axis transformations. A path between positions defines a journey operator as the product of per-axis transformations along that path. They prove that composition and movement across axes are path-independent iff axis transformations commute. Under toral-frame symmetry, cocycle, bilinearity, and norm-preservation assumptions, the pairwise scoring rule must be block-wise rotations. They then design JoFormer, a value aggregation model, linking it to attention and SSMs.
AI.result: The framework recovers RoPE and its multi-dimensional variants when transformations are fixed, and yields content-adaptive positional biases when transformations depend on data. The theoretical analysis proves path-independence conditions and the necessity of block-wise rotation scoring rules. JoFormer is introduced and initial experiments across vision, language, and length generalization show observable practical effects.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a principled foundation for multi-axis structured data modeling, explaining why RoPE-like methods are natural. JoFormer demonstrates that these inductive biases translate to practical benefits, suggesting further exploration of content-adaptive positional encodings in attention and state-space models.

title: Online Handwriting Trajectory Reconstruction from Kinematic Sensors using Temporal Convolutional Network
summary: Handwriting with digital pens is a common way to facilitate human-computer interaction through the use of Online Handwriting (OH) trajectory reconstruction. In this work, we focus on a digital pen equipped with sensors from which one wants to reconstruct the OH trajectory. Such a pen allows to write on any surface and to get the digital trace, which can help learning to write, by writing on paper, and can be useful for many other applications such as collaborative meetings, etc. In this paper, we introduce a novel processing pipeline that maps the sensor signals of the pen to the corresponding OH trajectory. Notably, in order to tackle the difference of sampling rates between the pen and the tablet (which provides ground truth information), our preprocessing pipeline relies on Dynamic Time Warping to align the signals. We introduce a dedicated neural network architecture, inspired by a Temporal Convolutional Network, to reconstruct the online trajectory from the pen sensor signals. Finally, we also present a new benchmark dataset on which our method is evaluated both qualitatively and quantitatively, showing a notable improvement over its most notable competitor.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel processing pipeline using a Temporal Convolutional Network-inspired architecture and Dynamic Time Warping to reconstruct online handwriting trajectories from digital pen sensor signals, demonstrating superior performance on a new benchmark dataset.
AI.motivation: To enable online handwriting trajectory reconstruction from a digital pen equipped with sensors (allowing writing on any surface), which is useful for applications such as learning to write, collaborative meetings, and general human-computer interaction.
AI.method: A processing pipeline that: (1) uses Dynamic Time Warping to align signals between the pen (different sampling rate) and tablet (ground truth), (2) employs a neural network architecture inspired by Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to reconstruct the OH trajectory from pen sensor signals.
AI.result: The method shows notable improvement over its most notable competitor, evaluated both qualitatively and quantitatively on a new benchmark dataset.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TCN-based pipeline with DTW-based alignment effectively reconstructs online handwriting trajectories from digital pen sensors, outperforming existing approaches.

title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution
summary: Large language model agents often encounter related yet distinct tasks that share reusable solution patterns. Yet standard agentic reinforcement learning treats tasks as independent episodes, while existing approaches to skill learning either focus on repeated attempts of one task or use pipelines with multiple stages that entangle extraction, retrieval, and execution. We introduce SkillRise, a unified reinforcement learning framework for learning skills across tasks. SkillRise organizes related instances into progressively challenging sequences and uses a single policy to alternate between task solving and curating an evolving skill document passed directly to the next task. Decoupled credit assignment across tasks supervises solving with the current task outcome and curation with discounted downstream outcomes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld show that SkillRise achieves the strongest Pass@1 performance among the compared methods, with gains over the strongest baseline ranging from 2.3 to 8.5 percentage points. Although trained across distinct tasks, its learned curation policy remains effective for repeated attempts on the same task. Further analysis reveals scaling at test time across tasks: performance improves with longer sequences of related tasks even when each task is attempted only once. This trend suggests that SkillRise reuses transferable skills across tasks rather than benefiting from repeated sampling of the same task. SkillRise further retains strong performance while substantially reducing the runtime overhead of skill learning pipelines with multiple stages. Together, these results provide a simple and efficient training paradigm for LLM agents to extract, refine, and reuse transferable skills across tasks.

AI.tldr: SkillRise is a unified RL framework that enables LLM agents to learn transferable skills across related tasks by organizing them into progressive sequences, using a single policy that alternates between solving tasks and curating an evolving skill document, achieving strong performance gains (2.3–8.5 pp) over baselines on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld while reducing runtime overhead.
AI.motivation: LLM agents face related but distinct tasks with reusable solution patterns, yet existing approaches treat tasks independently (standard agentic RL) or use multi-stage pipelines that entangle extraction, retrieval, and execution, lacking a unified framework for skill learning across tasks.
AI.method: SkillRise organizes related tasks into progressively challenging sequences, employs a single policy to alternate between task solving and curating an evolving skill document passed to subsequent tasks, and uses decoupled credit assignment—supervising solving with current task outcome and curation with discounted downstream outcomes.
AI.result: SkillRise achieves the strongest Pass@1 performance on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld, with gains of 2.3–8.5 pp over the strongest baseline. Its learned curation policy remains effective for repeated attempts on the same task. Performance scales with longer sequences of related tasks, indicating reuse of transferable skills rather than benefit from repeated sampling. SkillRise also substantially reduces runtime overhead of multi-stage skill learning pipelines.
AI.conclusion: SkillRise provides a simple and efficient training paradigm for LLM agents to extract, refine, and reuse transferable skills across tasks, outperforming existing methods while being more computationally efficient.

title: FedTopo: Relation-Level Topology Sharing for Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ICDE 2027 (first submission round)
summary: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative learning over decentralized data silos without centralizing raw data. However, heterogeneous local architectures often induce non-aligned representation spaces, making it difficult to transfer global knowledge across silos. Existing paradigms share this knowledge as model parameters, distilled predictions, or class prototypes, yet all encode it in an absolute space that must be aligned across clients. Heterogeneous backbones break this alignment, so the shared knowledge becomes unreliable and misleads local training. We propose FedTopo, a relation-level framework that encodes global knowledge as class relation topology, capturing how classes relate within each client rather than where they lie in feature space. Each client builds its relation topology from local prototypes and uploads it with class statistics. The server then aggregates these relations in a reliability-aware manner that down-weights weakly supported ones, and broadcasts the global topology to clients. The global topology guides local training by emphasizing topology-similar negative classes. Experiments on three datasets under eight heterogeneous backbones show that FedTopo consistently outperforms parameter-, distillation-, and prototype-sharing baselines, with low communication and no inference overhead. Our code is available at https://github.com/Zhaoyang-Ma/FedTopo.

AI.tldr: FedTopo is a relation-level federated learning framework that encodes global knowledge as class relation topology instead of absolute representations, enabling effective knowledge transfer across heterogeneous client backbones.
AI.motivation: Heterogeneous local architectures in federated learning cause non-aligned representation spaces, making traditional parameter-, distillation-, and prototype-sharing methods unreliable as they encode knowledge in an absolute space that breaks alignment across clients.
AI.method: Each client builds a class relation topology from local prototypes and uploads it with class statistics; the server aggregates these relations via reliability-aware weighting and broadcasts the global topology; local training is guided by emphasizing topology-similar negative classes.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms parameter-, distillation-, and prototype-sharing baselines across three datasets and eight heterogeneous backbones, with low communication cost and no inference overhead.
AI.conclusion: Encoding global knowledge as class relation topology rather than absolute-space representations effectively addresses the alignment problem in heterogeneous federated learning.

title: Multimodal fusion of visual and morphometric features for avian bone classification
summary: Artificial intelligence has shown considerable potential for archaeological applications, yet its use in zooarchaeology remains limited, particularly for the identification of avian skeletal remains. This study presents a proof-of-concept multimodal framework that integrates convolutional neural network-based image analysis with osteometric measurements for the classification of bird bones. Using a dataset of more than 10,000 images from multiple museum and research collections, two classification tasks were investigated: skeletal element identification and family-level taxonomic classification. Prior to classification, images were automatically segmented using a two-stage pipeline combining BiRefNet and SAM2. Visual features extracted with a pre-trained EfficientNet_V2_S backbone were fused with standardized morphometric data through a feature-level multimodal architecture. The model achieved 86% accuracy on the test set for bone-type classification, demonstrating reliable recognition of skeletal elements. Family-level classification proved more challenging, reaching 51% top-1 accuracy but 75% top-3 accuracy, indicating that correct taxa were frequently included among the most probable predictions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining visual and morphometric information within a unified deep-learning framework and establish a methodological baseline for future AI-assisted zooarchaeological identification. The approach contributes to ongoing efforts to develop scalable, interpretable, and archaeologically meaningful tools for the study of avian remains.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multimodal deep-learning framework combining CNN-based image analysis (EfficientNet_V2_S) with osteometric measurements for classifying bird bones, achieving 86% accuracy for skeletal element identification and 75% top-3 accuracy for family-level taxonomic classification using a dataset of over 10,000 images.
AI.motivation: AI use in zooarchaeology, especially for avian skeletal remains identification, remains limited despite its broader archaeological potential. A scalable, interpretable method is needed to assist zooarchaeological identification.
AI.method: A multimodal framework integrating a pre-trained EfficientNet_V2_S CNN for visual feature extraction with standardized osteometric measurements via feature-level fusion. Images were pre-processed with a two-stage segmentation pipeline (BiRefNet + SAM2). Two classification tasks were evaluated: skeletal element identification and family-level taxonomy.
AI.result: 86% accuracy on bone-type classification; 51% top-1 and 75% top-3 accuracy on family-level classification.
AI.conclusion: Combining visual and morphometric data in a unified deep-learning framework is feasible for zooarchaeological bird bone identification, establishing a methodological baseline for future AI-assisted tools.

title: Forecasting Trajectory-Level Safety Risks in Black-Box Multi-Turn Interactions
summary: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from standalone assistants into autonomous agents, ensuring their safety requires shifting beyond pointwise risk assessment to understand how risks emerge and unfold over long-horizon trajectories. In multi-turn interactions, malicious intent can be decomposed across seemingly harmless turns and gradually reconstructed through interaction trajectories, eventually resulting in safety failures. Existing safeguards remain largely reactive, detecting manifested violations while lacking the ability to predict latent risk evolution and enable preemptive prevention. To address this limitation, we propose Recast, a safety risk forecasting framework that advances LLM safeguarding beyond turn-level violation detection to trajectory-level risk prediction. Recast first retrieves risk-relevant evidence from both short-term dialogue progression and long-term historical context via a dual-scale trajectory view. It then models compositional risk evolution by capturing the current risk configuration and its temporal dynamics. Finally, a causal temporal encoder learns latent risk evolution patterns and predicts the distribution of future risk emergence turns. Extensive experiments across 7 risk categories show that Recast predicts 88.3% of future safety failures with an average lead time of 2.41 turns, while maintaining a false alarm rate of 12.3%, showcasing the effectiveness of trajectory-level forecasting in identifying emerging risks before safety violations occur.

AI.tldr: Recast is a safety risk forecasting framework that predicts future safety failures in multi-turn LLM agent interactions by modeling compositional risk evolution over trajectories, achieving 88.3% prediction accuracy with an average lead time of 2.41 turns.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM safeguards are reactive, detecting already-manifested safety violations but lacking the ability to predict latent risk evolution across long-horizon trajectories where malicious intent can be decomposed across seemingly harmless turns.
AI.method: Recast employs a dual-scale trajectory view to retrieve risk-relevant evidence from short-term dialogue and long-term context, models compositional risk evolution via current risk configuration and temporal dynamics, and uses a causal temporal encoder to learn latent risk patterns and predict future risk emergence turns.
AI.result: Across 7 risk categories, Recast predicts 88.3% of future safety failures with an average lead time of 2.41 turns and a false alarm rate of 12.3%.
AI.conclusion: Trajectory-level forecasting is effective for identifying emerging risks before safety violations occur, shifting LLM safeguarding from reactive detection to preemptive prevention.

title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation
summary: Recent game world models can generate visually realistic and interactive environments conditioned on player actions. However, games are not defined by pixels alone; they are governed by explicit mechanics, namely state-dependent rules that control health reduction, skill activation, and game termination. These mechanics depend on precise internal states, such as health points, skill meters, and timers, which are tightly coupled with visual observations and determine how gameplay evolves. Without modeling these state dynamics, existing game world models may generate visually plausible rollouts but violate the underlying game rules. In this paper, we propose StatePlay, a novel state-aware game world model that jointly predicts visual content and game states to promote mechanics-consistent generation. StatePlay adopts a mixture-of-transformers (MoT)-style architecture that preserves specialized visual and state representations while enabling cross-modal interaction, allowing predicted states to guide frame generation. Each branch is further optimized with a distinct objective suited to its modality. Experiments show that StatePlay achieves an average normalized L1 distance below 0.06 for state prediction. Furthermore, compared with models without explicit state modeling, our method improves mechanics fidelity in generated game rollouts by 18.6%. Overall, our work highlights the importance of state-aware game world modeling and advances beyond pixel-level realism toward complete and mechanically faithful game generation.

AI.tldr: StatePlay is a state-aware game world model using a mixture-of-transformers architecture that jointly predicts visual content and game states, improving mechanics fidelity by 18.6% with state prediction error below 0.06 normalized L1 distance.
AI.motivation: Existing game world models generate visually plausible rollouts but fail to model explicit game mechanics (e.g., health, skill meters, timers), leading to violations of underlying game rules.
AI.method: StatePlay uses a mixture-of-transformers (MoT) architecture with specialized visual and state branches that preserve modality-specific representations while enabling cross-modal interaction, where predicted states guide frame generation. Each branch is optimized with a distinct objective suited to its modality.
AI.result: StatePlay achieves an average normalized L1 distance below 0.06 for state prediction and improves mechanics fidelity by 18.6% compared to models without explicit state modeling.
AI.conclusion: State-aware game world modeling advances beyond pixel-level realism toward complete and mechanically faithful game generation.

title: Budget-Aware LLM Discovery via Cost-Calibrated Frontier Utility
summary: Large language models increasingly support scientific and algorithmic discovery through inference-time search over evaluated candidates. Existing adaptive discovery controllers assign credit based only on score progress, even though prompt length, retries, and guidance calls cause search actions to incur different token costs. We prove that cost-blind credit can forfeit all but a vanishing fraction of attainable quality as frontiers multiply and costs diverge. Under a fixed search-side token budget, the controller must decide which frontier is improving and whether its gain justifies the realized cost before the budget is exhausted. We introduce \textbf{CostAda}, a cost-calibrated adaptive controller built around \emph{cost-calibrated frontier utility}. The utility values frontier progress relative to realized action cost and conditions that credit on the remaining budget. CostAda uses this signal to control local exploration intensity, frontier allocation, and budgeted tactic intervention. Cost and remaining budget therefore shape the search rather than serving only as accounting variables or a stopping rule. CostAda reaches the strongest baseline's full-budget quality with at most half the budget on twelve of sixteen benchmark--backbone pairs while achieving the strongest mean final quality on all eight benchmarks under GLM-5 and GPT-5.4.

AI.tldr: CostAda is a cost-calibrated adaptive controller for LLM-based search that accounts for varying token costs of different search actions, proving cost-blind credit allocation forfeits quality as frontiers multiply. It achieves baselines' full-budget quality with half the budget on 12/16 pairs and strongest mean quality on all 8 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing adaptive discovery controllers assign credit based only on score progress, ignoring that search actions (prompt length, retries, guidance calls) incur different token costs. This cost-blind approach forfeits quality as frontiers multiply and costs diverge.
AI.method: CostAda uses cost-calibrated frontier utility that values frontier progress relative to realized action cost and conditions credit on the remaining budget. It controls local exploration intensity, frontier allocation, and budgeted tactic intervention, making cost and remaining budget shape the search itself.
AI.result: CostAda reaches the strongest baseline's full-budget quality with at most half the budget on 12 of 16 benchmark–backbone pairs, and achieves the strongest mean final quality on all 8 benchmarks under GLM-5 and GPT-5.4.
AI.conclusion: Cost-calibrated adaptive control significantly improves search efficiency under token budgets, proving that integrating cost signals into credit assignment rather than treating them as accounting variables yields better quality-cost Pareto frontiers.

title: Long-Tailed 3D Point Cloud Dataset Distillation
summary: Dataset distillation compresses large-scale datasets into compact synthetic sets while preserving their training utility, enabling efficient 3D point cloud training. Current point cloud dataset distillation methods only tackle geometric and representation challenges while ignoring the distributional imbalance prevalent in point cloud datasets where both training and test splits follow long-tailed class distributions. To our knowledge, we present the first study on long-tailed point cloud dataset distillation. Rather than focusing primarily on geometric and representation properties or simply constructing a class-balanced synthetic set, our framework explicitly accounts for long-tailed class distributions via two core modules. First, we design Adaptive Synthetic Budgeting to allocate class-wise synthetic budgets according to class quantity and the expected benefit of additional synthetic samples. Given the allocated budgets, we further design 3D Long-Tailed Distribution Matching to optimize synthetic point clouds through Global-Local Feature Alignment and Prior-Aware Supervision. The former preserves both global class distributions and diverse intra-class structures, while the latter provides class-dependent expert supervision to keep tail-class samples recognizable while maintaining diverse head-class patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, lifting classification accuracy by 7.0 points on ShapeNet55 against state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: First study on long-tailed point cloud dataset distillation, introducing Adaptive Synthetic Budgeting and 3D Long-Tailed Distribution Matching to handle class imbalance, achieving 7.0% accuracy improvement on ShapeNet55.
AI.motivation: Existing point cloud dataset distillation methods overlook the distributional imbalance (long-tailed class distributions) prevalent in real-world point cloud datasets, leading to degraded performance on tail classes.
AI.method: Two core modules: (1) Adaptive Synthetic Budgeting - allocates class-wise synthetic budgets based on class quantity and expected marginal benefit; (2) 3D Long-Tailed Distribution Matching - optimizes synthetic point clouds via Global-Local Feature Alignment (preserves global class distributions and intra-class structures) and Prior-Aware Supervision (provides class-dependent expert supervision for tail-class recognition).
AI.result: Lifts classification accuracy by 7.0 points on ShapeNet55 against state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling long-tailed distributions in dataset distillation significantly improves performance, demonstrating the importance of addressing class imbalance beyond geometric and representation challenges in point cloud distillation.

title: Kairos: Numerically Robust News Recommendation under Item Cold-Start via Cholesky-based LinUCB
comment: English preprint. The German version was peer-reviewed and accepted at SKILL 2026 (Gesellschaft für Informatik)
summary: Algorithmic news personalization in regional markets often fails because modern deep learning models require massive interaction data while real-world news has a short Time-to-Live (TTL < 48 h) and shallow article pools. This structural item cold-start deprives collaborative filtering of the data needed for robust modeling. This paper presents Project Kairos, a framework that bridges this data scarcity through a contextual online learning approach (LinUCB). To ensure numerical integrity for continuous operation, Kairos replaces error-prone Sherman-Morrison inversions with direct rank-1 updates of Cholesky factors. This preserves the positive definiteness of the covariance matrix even under ill-conditioned data scenarios. Simultaneously, Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) integration addresses inference latency. Empirical evaluations based on the Tagesschau API demonstrate that exploiting semantic redundancy in the feature space achieves a 4.85-fold efficiency gain without significantly compromising ranking precision. Kairos thus provides a blueprint for high-performance recommendation systems in resource- and data-constrained environments.

AI.tldr: Project Kairos addresses the cold-start problem in algorithmic news personalization by combining LinUCB contextual bandits with Cholesky factor updates (instead of Sherman-Morrison) and Matryoshka Representation Learning, achieving 4.85× efficiency gains on real news data while maintaining ranking precision.
AI.motivation: Modern deep recommendation models fail in regional news personalization because news has a short TTL (<48h) and small article pools, creating a structural item cold-start problem where collaborative filtering lacks sufficient interaction data.
AI.method: Kairos uses LinUCB (contextual online learning) with two key innovations: (1) replacing Sherman-Morrison inversions with direct rank-1 Cholesky factor updates to maintain numerical stability and positive definiteness, and (2) integrating Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) to reduce inference latency by exploiting semantic feature redundancy.
AI.result: Evaluation on Tagesschau API data shows a 4.85-fold efficiency gain without significant ranking precision loss.
AI.conclusion: Kairos provides a practical blueprint for deploying high-performance recommendation systems in resource- and data-constrained environments.

title: Searching for Robust Augmentations to Improve Out-of-Domain Generalization in Dermoscopic Skin Cancer Classification
summary: Background/Objectives: Dermoscopic skin lesion classifiers often lose accuracy under domain shift across imaging devices, illumination, and capture artifacts. We study how data augmentation improves the robustness of a binary malignant-versus-non-malignant classifier, with emphasis on out-of-domain (OOD) generalization. Methods: Single augmentations, photometric combinations, and composite policies were searched on a multi-source ISIC Archive collection with Derm7pt, using a ConvNeXt-Large backbone and ROC-AUC. Splits were made at the lesion-ID level, and HAM10000 and ISIC 2019-2020 were held out as a predominantly source-disjoint OOD test. Results: The largest OOD gain came from the mix policy, and photometric transformations dominated the most useful OOD operations. On an expanded pool from the same held-out sources the gain was +0.053 (95% CI +0.045 to +0.061, p<0.001), consistent across four training seeds (per-seed ROC-AUC: baseline 0.761-0.775, mix 0.806-0.829). On a small independent clinical collection, single-checkpoint sensitivity rose from 0.591 to 0.818, but this rested on 22 malignant cases and did not persist across seeds. Conclusions: Augmentations modelling real sources of domain shift can matter more than maximizing in-domain accuracy. Because the policy was selected on the same sources used to evaluate it, a source-disjoint selection protocol is needed before this effect size can be read as unbiased.

AI.tldr: Data augmentation, especially photometric transformations and mix policies, improves OOD generalization of a dermoscopic skin lesion classifier, but source-disjoint selection is needed for unbiased effect estimation.
AI.motivation: Dermoscopic skin lesion classifiers degrade under domain shift caused by differences in imaging devices, illumination, and capture artifacts. The authors study how data augmentation can improve out-of-domain (OOD) generalization for a binary malignant-vs-non-malignant classifier.
AI.method: Single augmentations, photometric combinations, and composite policies were searched on a multi-source ISIC Archive collection with Derm7pt. A ConvNeXt-Large backbone was used with ROC-AUC evaluation. Lesion-ID-level splits were made; HAM10000 and ISIC 2019-2020 served as source-disjoint OOD test sets.
AI.result: The mix policy yielded the largest OOD gain; photometric transformations dominated the most useful operations. On held-out sources, gain was +0.053 (95% CI +0.045 to +0.061, p<0.001) across seeds (baseline 0.761-0.775, mix 0.806-0.829). On a small clinical set, sensitivity rose from 0.591 to 0.818 but relied on 22 malignant cases and was not seed-consistent.
AI.conclusion: Augmentations modeling real domain shifts matter more than maximizing in-domain accuracy. However, the policy was selected on the same sources used for evaluation, so a source-disjoint selection protocol is required before the effect size can be considered unbiased.

title: Tight Generalization Bound for AdaBoost
summary: In this paper we show that the generalization error of AdaBoost is $Θ\big(\tfrac{d\ln(nγ^{2}/d)}{nγ^2}+\tfrac{\ln(1/δ)}{n}\big)$, where $γ$ is the advantage guaranteed by the weak learner, $d$ is the VC-dimension of the class containing the weak hypotheses, $n$ is the sample size, and $δ$ is the confidence parameter. The contribution of this paper is the upper bound; the matching lower bound follows from prior work. The upper bound proof follows by combining the known fact that AdaBoost outputs a voting classifier whose voting function has zero empirical $γ/2$-margin loss with what is, to the best of our knowledge, a new margin-based generalization bound for voting classifiers.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes the generalization error of AdaBoost as Θ((d ln(nγ²/d))/(nγ²) + (ln(1/δ))/n), proving a tight upper bound that matches prior lower bounds.
AI.motivation: To precisely characterize the generalization error of AdaBoost in terms of the weak learner's advantage γ, the VC-dimension d of the weak hypothesis class, sample size n, and confidence parameter δ.
AI.method: Combines the known property that AdaBoost produces a voting classifier with zero empirical γ/2-margin loss with a new margin-based generalization bound for voting classifiers.
AI.result: Proves an upper bound of Θ((d ln(nγ²/d))/(nγ²) + (ln(1/δ))/n) for AdaBoost's generalization error, which matches the lower bound from prior work.
AI.conclusion: The generalization error of AdaBoost is now tightly characterized, showing the dependency on the weak learner's advantage and the VC-dimension of the weak hypothesis class.

title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?
summary: Multimodal large language models increasingly use sketches, annotations, tools, and intermediate images during reasoning, but it remains unclear whether they truly rely on these visual states. Existing benchmarks are limited both by task collections with narrow coverage or partially text-solvable samples and by evaluations that emphasize final answers without diagnosing how intermediate visual states are generated, rendered, and used. We introduce See2Think, a unified evaluation framework comprising See2ThinkBench and Visual Action-of-Thought (VAoT). See2ThinkBench contains 1,200 open-ended, visually dependent problems across 12 task categories spanning 2D structured, 3D scene, and real-world reasoning. VAoT records textual thoughts, visual actions, rendered states, and subsequent reasoning under four controlled inference settings. Evaluating representative proprietary and open-source multimodal models, we find that visual reasoning is strongly model- and environment-dependent, with no single setting consistently dominating across tasks. Process analysis further shows that models usually select relevant visual operations, while faithful rendering remains the clearest bottleneck and high feedback uptake does not necessarily translate into accuracy gains. Under task-relevant corrupted feedback, models exhibit behavioral dependence on visual states, with accuracy dropping by over 10 percentage points in controlled interventions.

AI.tldr: See2Think is a unified evaluation framework (benchmark + process analysis method) that tests whether multimodal LLMs truly rely on intermediate visual states (sketches, annotations, tools, rendered images) during reasoning. It reveals that visual reasoning is model- and task-dependent, faithful rendering is the main bottleneck, and corrupting visual feedback significantly degrades accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks have limited coverage, contain text-solvable samples, and only evaluate final answers without diagnosing how intermediate visual states are generated, rendered, and used, leaving it unclear whether models truly rely on visual states during reasoning.
AI.method: See2ThinkBench (1,200 open-ended, visually dependent problems across 12 task categories in 2D structured, 3D scene, and real-world reasoning) plus Visual Action-of-Thought (VAoT) which records textual thoughts, visual actions, rendered states, and reasoning under four controlled inference settings.
