Our work establishes the first connection between autoregressive video drifting and model internal representations, adopts erank as a quantitative metric for error accumulation, reveals counterintuitive scaling limitations for video world models, and presents a simple yet effective regularization strategy to improve long video generation robustness.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies that error accumulation in autoregressive video world models stems from dimensional collapse of hidden representations (effective rank drop), finds that training data scaling cannot fix this issue, and proposes a lightweight video representation regularization method to stabilize latent representations, achieving significant improvements on VBench metrics.
AI.motivation: Video diffusion world models suffer from severe error accumulation during long autoregressive generation, degrading frame quality over time. The underlying mechanism of this compounding error and how to achieve stable long-horizon generation remain unresolved.
AI.method: The authors investigate internal representation dynamics and discover that compounding error is tightly coupled with dimensional collapse of hidden representations, measured by effective rank (erank). They propose video representation regularization, a lightweight training constraint that stabilizes latent representations to suppress iterative error accumulation.
AI.result: Compared with Diffusion Forcing, the proposed method improves Aesthetic Quality from 38.65 to 55.56 and Imaging Quality from 44.37 to 72.08 on VBench.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the first connection between autoregressive video drifting and model internal representations, adopts erank as a quantitative metric for error accumulation, reveals counterintuitive scaling limitations for video world models, and presents a simple yet effective regularization strategy for long video generation.

title: CoCaRS: Correlation Calibration-Based Redundancy Suppression for Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation
summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables a compact student model to learn from a powerful teacher and has become an effective paradigm for model compression. The emergence of diverse model architectures has extended KD from homogeneous to heterogeneous settings. However, differences in architectural inductive biases between the teacher and student models often result in substantial representation discrepancies, limiting the effectiveness of direct knowledge transfer. Recently, redundancy suppression has offered a new perspective on heterogeneous KD by preserving cross-architecture invariance and reducing feature redundancy through decorrelation of teacher-student feature correlations. Nevertheless, this formulation may weaken useful structural information through uniform decorrelation, while a fixed coefficient may make the effective contribution of redundancy suppression sensitive to teacher-student pairs and training stages. To address these problems, Correlation Calibration-based Redundancy Suppression (CoCaRS) is proposed to better retain structural information while suppressing redundancy and reduce sensitivity to coefficient settings across teacher-student pairs and training stages. Specifically, CoCaRS calibrates feature decorrelation through Confusion Evidence Estimation (CEE) and Strength Allocation Control (SAC), which respectively capture reliable semantic relations for correlation estimation and preserve discriminative structure during decorrelation. Adaptive Coefficient Regulation (ACR) further regulates the contribution of the calibrated redundancy suppression objective according to its relative loss scale, reducing sensitivity to coefficient settings. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K validate the effectiveness of CoCaRS in improving distillation performance and reducing sensitivity to coefficient settings. Code will be released soon.

AI.tldr: CoCaRS proposes Correlation Calibration-based Redundancy Suppression for heterogeneous knowledge distillation, using Confusion Evidence Estimation, Strength Allocation Control, and Adaptive Coefficient Regulation to better preserve structural information while reducing representation discrepancies between teacher and student models.
AI.motivation: Existing heterogeneous KD methods using redundancy suppression may weaken useful structural information through uniform decorrelation, and fixed coefficients make the contribution of redundancy suppression sensitive to different teacher-student pairs and training stages.
AI.method: CoCaRS includes three components: (1) Confusion Evidence Estimation (CEE) for capturing reliable semantic relations, (2) Strength Allocation Control (SAC) for preserving discriminative structure during decorrelation, and (3) Adaptive Coefficient Regulation (ACR) that adjusts the redundancy suppression objective's contribution based on relative loss scale.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K show CoCaRS improves distillation performance and reduces sensitivity to coefficient settings.
AI.conclusion: CoCaRS effectively addresses limitations of prior redundancy suppression approaches in heterogeneous knowledge distillation by calibrating feature decorrelation and adaptively regulating suppression strength.

title: Object Detection for Autonomous Driving in Chinese Rural Scenes: An Experimental Study on Real-Synthetic Data Mixing and Model Evaluation
summary: Currently, autonomous driving object detection models face significant data scarcity and generalization challenges when navigating complex Chinese rural traffic scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose a novel real-synthetic mixed object detection dataset tailored specifically for Chinese rural roads and systematically evaluate the performance of 13 mainstream detectors under different real-to-synthetic data ratios, thereby providing empirical evidence for model selection and data strategy design in rural autonomous driving scenarios. Our dataset combines real-world images captured in Weishi County, Henan Province, with parameterized virtual scenes generated via Unreal Engine. To accurately reflect the unique realities of rural traffic, we define a comprehensive 14-category object system encompassing region-specific elements such as electric tricycles, low-speed vehicles (LSVs), and roadside stalls. Under a unified training protocol, we systematically evaluate 13 mainstream detectors -- spanning the YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLO11, and YOLO26 series, as well as RT-DETR-L -- across three data configurations: an all-real baseline, a 1:0.5 real-to-virtual mix, and a 1:1 mix. Experimental results demonstrate that a moderate injection of synthetic data (1:0.5 ratio) effectively enhances detection performance, with YOLO11m achieving the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.758. However, a higher proportion of synthetic data (1:1) introduces domain shifts that offset the benefits of data scaling. While most models reliably identify distinct local vehicles, significant perceptual bottlenecks remain for long-tail, non-standard objects like stalls and railings. This research provides crucial empirical evidence and novel insights for model selection and synthetic data strategies, facilitating the practical deployment of autonomous driving perception systems in rural areas.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel real-synthetic mixed dataset for autonomous driving object detection on Chinese rural roads, evaluates 13 mainstream detectors across different real-to-synthetic data ratios, and finds that a moderate (1:0.5) synthetic data injection improves detection performance (YOLO11m achieves 0.758 mAP@0.5), while excessive synthetic data (1:1) causes domain shift degradation.
AI.motivation: Autonomous driving object detection models face significant data scarcity and generalization challenges in complex Chinese rural traffic scenarios due to the lack of region-specific datasets.
AI.method: A real-synthetic mixed dataset was created combining real-world images from Weishi County, Henan Province with parameterized virtual scenes from Unreal Engine, using a 14-category object system (including electric tricycles, LSVs, roadside stalls). 13 mainstream detectors (YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLO11, YOLO26 series, and RT-DETR-L) were evaluated under three data configurations: all-real, 1:0.5 real-to-virtual mix, and 1:1 mix.
AI.result: A moderate 1:0.5 synthetic data ratio enhances detection performance; YOLO11m achieves the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.758. However, a 1:1 ratio causes domain shift that offsets data scaling benefits. Most models reliably detect local vehicles but struggle with long-tail, non-standard objects like stalls and railings.
AI.conclusion: This research provides empirical evidence and insights for model selection and synthetic data strategies, facilitating practical deployment of autonomous driving perception systems in rural areas.

title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret for Online Convex Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise
summary: We study online convex optimization (OCO) in non-stationary environments under heavy-tailed noise, where the stochastic gradient oracle admits only a finite $p$-th central moment for some $p \in (1, 2]$. While static regret is well-understood, achieving universal dynamic regret in a parameter-free manner remains an open challenge. We resolve this by proposing \textbf{HT-PAder}, a parameter-free algorithm combining restarted AdaGrad experts over a geometric pool of block lengths with a pathwise meta-algorithm, \textbf{AdaGrad-Hedge}, which requires no moment conditions on meta-losses. For a domain of diameter $D$, Lipschitz constant $G$, noise level $σ$, and comparator path length $P_T$, HT-PAder achieves an expected universal dynamic regret of \[ \widetilde O\left( GD\sqrt{T(1+P_T/D)} + σD T^{1/p}(1+P_T/D)^{(p-1)/p} \right). \] The algorithm does not require prior knowledge of any of these problem parameters. Even in the special case of finite variance ($p=2$), HT-PAder provides the first parameter-free minimax universal dynamic regret guarantee. We also prove a matching lower bound, establishing the optimality of the path-length exponent.

AI.tldr: HT-PAder is a parameter-free algorithm for online convex optimization in non-stationary environments with heavy-tailed noise, achieving minimax-optimal universal dynamic regret without requiring prior knowledge of problem parameters.
AI.motivation: Static regret for OCO with heavy-tailed noise is well-understood, but achieving universal dynamic regret in a parameter-free manner (without knowing domain diameter, Lipschitz constant, noise level, or comparator path length) remained an open challenge.
AI.method: HT-PAder combines restarted AdaGrad experts over a geometric pool of block lengths with a pathwise meta-algorithm called AdaGrad-Hedge, which requires no moment conditions on meta-losses.
AI.result: Expected universal dynamic regret of Õ(GD√(T(1+PT/D)) + σD T^{1/p}(1+PT/D)^{(p-1)/p}). A matching lower bound is also provided, establishing optimality of the path-length exponent.
AI.conclusion: HT-PAder provides the first parameter-free minimax universal dynamic regret guarantee even in the finite variance (p=2) case, and the lower bound confirms optimality.

title: ScratchSim: A Procedural Synthetic Data Pipeline for Surface Scratch Detection
summary: While automated defect detection such as the detection of surface scratched is an important aspect in industrial quality control, the scarcity of annotated defect data make this task challenging. This paper presents a procedural rendering pipeline that generates large-scale annotated synthetic training data using BlenderProc, with configurable material appearance, camera modes, and domain randomization, producing automatic COCO-format annotations. To show the potential of our approach, we evaluate four training strategies, namely synthetic-only, real-only, mixed, and fine-tuning from synthetic weights, across two objects with different material properties and three lightweight edge-deployable detectors, YOLOX, YOLO26, and LW-DETR. Our evaluation show that fine-tuning from synthetic weights consistently outperforms real-only training, and that mixed training effectively recovers performance under scarce real-data conditions, with findings validated across both convolutional and transformer-based architectures. The proposed approach enables scalable defect detection without the burden of large real annotated datasets, making it practical for on-device industrial inspection. The pipeline scripts, 3D model, and both synthetic and real annotated scratch datasets for a glossy toy Ferrari car will be made available through the project website upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: A procedural rendering pipeline (BlenderProc) generates large-scale synthetic annotated data for industrial defect detection, achieving strong results by fine-tuning from synthetic weights and mixed training, outperforming real-only training on edge-deployable detectors.
AI.motivation: Scarcity of annotated defect data makes automated industrial quality control challenging; the paper aims to eliminate the burden of large real annotated datasets.
AI.method: Procedural rendering pipeline using BlenderProc with configurable materials, camera modes, domain randomization, and automatic COCO-format annotations; evaluated on four training strategies (synthetic-only, real-only, mixed, fine-tuning from synthetic weights) across two objects and three lightweight detectors (YOLOX, YOLO26, LW-DETR).
AI.result: Fine-tuning from synthetic weights consistently outperforms real-only training; mixed training effectively recovers performance under scarce real-data conditions; findings validated across convolutional and transformer-based architectures.
AI.conclusion: The approach enables scalable defect detection without large real annotated datasets, making it practical for on-device industrial inspection.

title: Single-Beat Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using Ear-PPG and ECG with a Lightweight Hybrid Learning Framework
summary: Continuous cuffless blood pressure (BP) monitoring remains challenging due to motion artifacts, physiological variability, and the limited robustness of conventional pulse transit time (PTT) models under dynamic conditions. Many prior approaches rely on multi-second windows to stabilize estimation, an assumption that is frequently violated during real-world monitoring with intermittent signal corruption. Here, we show that discriminative BP-related information is preserved at the single-beat level and present a lightweight multi-modal wearable framework for continuous BP estimation. The system integrates synchronized chest electrocardiography (ECG) and ear-clip reflectance photoplethysmography, each co-located with a 6-axis inertial measurement unit to provide motion context. We introduce a hybrid learning architecture in which a one-dimensional convolutional neural network extracts a 64-dimensional embedding from individual PPG beats and fuses it with 30 physiology-grounded features, including PTT statistics and heart rate variability, followed by LightGBM regression. The method was evaluated using a multi-phase stress protocol ($n=10$) and the PulseDB public dataset with subject-disjoint validation. Across 30 independent runs, the model achieved mean absolute errors of $4.02 \pm 0.21$~mmHg for systolic BP and $1.79 \pm 0.05$~mmHg for diastolic BP, corresponding to a 28.2\% reduction in combined MAE relative to baseline models. By enabling beat-wise estimation without long temporal context, this framework supports computationally efficient cuffless BP monitoring suitable for wearable deployment under practical resource constraints. The source code for this work is available at https://github.com/SYMBIOX-Lab/BP-wireless.

AI.tldr: A lightweight multi-modal wearable framework using single-beat ECG and PPG with hybrid CNN-LightGBM architecture achieves beat-wise BP estimation (SBP MAE: 4.02 mmHg, DBP MAE: 1.79 mmHg), reducing combined MAE by 28.2% over baselines without requiring multi-second temporal windows.
AI.motivation: Continuous cuffless BP monitoring is challenged by motion artifacts, physiological variability, and poor robustness of conventional PTT models under dynamic conditions; prior approaches rely on multi-second windows that fail during real-world monitoring with intermittent signal corruption.
AI.method: Hybrid learning architecture: 1D-CNN extracts 64-dimensional embedding from individual PPG beats, fused with 30 physiology-grounded features (PTT statistics, HRV), followed by LightGBM regression. System uses synchronized chest ECG and ear-clip reflectance PPG, each co-located with 6-axis IMU for motion context.
AI.result: Across 30 independent runs (multi-phase stress protocol + PulseDB public dataset, subject-disjoint validation): MAE of 4.02±0.21 mmHg for SBP and 1.79±0.05 mmHg for DBP, achieving 28.2% reduction in combined MAE relative to baseline models.
AI.conclusion: Beat-wise BP estimation is feasible without long temporal context, supporting computationally efficient cuffless BP monitoring suitable for wearable deployment under practical resource constraints.

title: SciFigAlign: Scoring Scientific Figures by Fine-tuned Alignment of Visuals with Manuscript Evidence
summary: Scientific figure assessment in peer review differs fundamentally from general image quality evaluation: a figure must be visually legible, faithfully support the manuscript's claims, and communicate evidence with a clear visual hierarchy. However, if we apply traditional image assessment methods to scientific figure quality assessment, limitations emerge: classic IQA models capture perceptual quality or aesthetics but cannot judge whether a figure serves the paper's scientific argument; CLIP-based methods assess generic image-text correspondence, yet lack understanding of manuscript context; and zero-shot LLM/VLM judges, when repurposed for figure scoring, often yield overly concentrated scores with limited fusion of visual and textual evidence. We introduce an annotated dataset of 3,857 scientific figures from peer-reviewed conference papers, each rated along four peer-review-oriented dimensions: Clarity, Relevance, Informativeness, and Structure. We propose SciFigAlign, a fine-tuned multimodal scorer that grounds figure quality assessment in manuscript evidence. Given a figure crop, caption, citing paragraphs, and light paper context, SciFigAlign fine-tunes CLIP and SciBERT end-to-end with per-modality cross-attention and CubeMLP fusion, jointly optimizing SmoothL1 regression with a within-paper ranking hinge loss. Under paper-level splits, SciFigAlign achieves a macro MAE of 0.3524 and a within-paper pairwise accuracy of 81.64% on the test set with n = 396, a 59% relative error reduction over the best LLM-as-judge baseline with MAE 0.864. Ablations confirm that manuscript-grounded inputs, citing-context denoising, and ranking supervision are all critical, showing that scientific figure assessment requires learned alignment between visual content and manuscript evidence rather than prompting alone, even with state-of-the-art VLMs.

AI.tldr: SciFigAlign is a fine-tuned multimodal scorer for scientific figure quality assessment that integrates visual content with manuscript evidence (caption, citing paragraphs, paper context) using CLIP and SciBERT with cross-attention and CubeMLP fusion, achieving 59% relative error reduction over LLM-as-judge baselines on a 3,857-figure dataset rated along Clarity, Relevance, Informativeness, and Structure dimensions.
AI.motivation: Scientific figure assessment in peer review differs fundamentally from general image quality evaluation: a figure must be visually legible, faithfully support claims, and communicate evidence with clear visual hierarchy. Existing methods (IQA, CLIP-based, zero-shot LLM/VLM) fail to capture manuscript-grounded scientific argument understanding.
AI.method: Introduced a dataset of 3,857 scientific figures rated on Clarity, Relevance, Informativeness, and Structure. Proposed SciFigAlign: fine-tunes CLIP and SciBERT end-to-end with per-modality cross-attention and CubeMLP fusion, jointly optimizing SmoothL1 regression with within-paper ranking hinge loss.
AI.result: SciFigAlign achieves macro MAE 0.3524 and within-paper pairwise accuracy 81.64% (test set n=396), a 59% relative error reduction over best LLM-as-judge baseline (MAE 0.864). Ablations confirm manuscript-grounded inputs, citing-context denoising, and ranking supervision are all critical.
AI.conclusion: Scientific figure assessment requires learned alignment between visual content and manuscript evidence rather than prompting alone, even with state-of-the-art VLMs.

title: Equilibrium Training of Energy-Based Models with Parallel Trajectory Tempering
summary: Energy-Based Models (EBMs) provide an interpretable framework for generative modeling of scientific data, but poor Markov Chain Monte Carlo mixing often limits their reliability. We introduce a training algorithm based on Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT), which exploits the continuity of the optimization path to maintain equilibrium sampling throughout learning. This enables stable and fast training on highly multimodal and data-scarce scientific datasets. Combined with reservoir sampling and adaptive optimization, PTT has a computational cost comparable to Persistent Contrastive Divergence, making it a practical replacement for standard training methods. It also provides direct estimates of thermalization times, equilibrium samples from trained models, and accurate log-likelihoods at essentially no additional cost. Experiments on Restricted Boltzmann Machines show that PTT consistently outperforms existing EBM training approaches. On discrete tabular data, it also surpasses state-of-the-art deep generative models, yielding higher-quality samples and greater robustness to overfitting and limited data. Our results make equilibrium maximum-likelihood training of EBMs practical and computationally efficient.

AI.tldr: Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT) is a training algorithm for Energy-Based Models that maintains equilibrium sampling throughout learning, enabling stable and efficient training on multimodal, data-scarce scientific datasets while outperforming existing EBM and deep generative model approaches.
AI.motivation: Energy-Based Models (EBMs) offer an interpretable framework for generative modeling of scientific data, but their reliability is limited by poor Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) mixing during training.
AI.method: The authors introduce Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT), which exploits the continuity of the optimization path to maintain equilibrium sampling throughout learning. It is combined with reservoir sampling and adaptive optimization, achieving computational cost comparable to Persistent Contrastive Divergence.
AI.result: PTT consistently outperforms existing EBM training approaches on Restricted Boltzmann Machines. On discrete tabular data, it surpasses state-of-the-art deep generative models, yielding higher-quality samples and greater robustness to overfitting and limited data.
AI.conclusion: PTT makes equilibrium maximum-likelihood training of EBMs practical and computationally efficient, providing direct estimates of thermalization times, equilibrium samples, and accurate log-likelihoods at essentially no additional cost.

title: Visual Credit Audit for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
summary: Closed yes/no spatial benchmarks can reward a correct answer even when the image adds little support beyond no-image contexts. Under a fixed forced-choice interface, Visual Credit Audit (VCA) separates two estimands: whether the benchmark image gives the model's declared decision more support than text-only and blank controls, and whether the model responds to relation-specific visual evidence. The first audit is training- and label-free and does not require an answer flip. Applying labels yields dependence-credited correctness (D-CC); on correct items, it equals same-control gold-aligned positive gain, while prediction alignment extends the audit to errors. Across four open MLLMs and two spatial benchmarks, 12.73-26.25% of decisions are correct yet uncredited. Matched same-split image permutation reduces D-CC by 21.25-47.80 points, with every paired 95% interval above zero. Fixed-pixel relation contrasts and a 3x3 evidence-source factorial show why null controls cannot identify relation response. Among controlled correct-but-uncredited agreement decisions, response to relation reversal spans 81.57-100.00%, while 32.11% pooled change answer. Independently audited outcomes on 108 geometry-compatible edits provide a bounded natural-image correspondence check. VCA thereby decomposes benchmark success into correctness, additional image support, and relation-consistent response.

AI.tldr: Visual Credit Audit (VCA) decomposes MLLM spatial benchmark performance into correctness, image support beyond no-image baselines, and relation-specific visual response, revealing 12.73-26.25% of correct decisions lack genuine visual credit.
AI.motivation: Closed yes/no spatial benchmarks may reward correct answers even when the image contributes little beyond no-image contexts, conflating language priors with genuine visual reasoning. Existing evaluation does not separate whether models rely on visual evidence or text-only shortcuts.
AI.method: VCA uses two audits: (1) training- and label-free comparison of model decision support from benchmark images vs. text-only and blank controls; (2) dependence-credited correctness (D-CC) via gold-aligned positive gain. Includes image permutation, relation reversal contrasts, and 3x3 evidence-source factorial design.
AI.result: Across four open MLLMs and two spatial benchmarks, 12.73-26.25% correct decisions lack visual credit. Same-split image permutation reduces D-CC by 21.25-47.80 points. Relation reversal yields 81.57-100% agreement among correct-but-uncredited decisions; 32.11% pooled change answer. Validated on 108 geometry-compatible edits.
AI.conclusion: VCA decomposes benchmark success into correctness, additional image support, and relation-consistent response, providing a principled framework to audit whether spatial benchmark performance reflects genuine visual understanding or text-driven shortcuts.

title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
summary: As LLM agents increasingly depend on diverse external services such as search engines, databases, and connectors, agent harnesses face a fundamental tool-selection challenge: acquiring too few tools leaves the task under-informed, while too many adds cost, context load, and privacy exposure. Routers and retrievers can rank candidate tools by relevance, but a ranking alone does not determine how many are worth selecting. Existing approaches leave acquisition under heterogeneous costs unaddressed. We formulate this decision as cost-aware marginal decision-focused stopping (CAM-DF) over ranked tool prefixes, with CAM-DF-lite as a compact interpretable variant. We train directly on the offline gap between stopping now and the best continuation: its sign labels the decision, its magnitude weights each error by the payoff at stake. We prove this objective is Bayes-aligned with the stopping target and that score-only rules are suboptimal under heterogeneous costs. We evaluate on 1,343 tasks across five tool-use domains. On $τ$-bench Retail, CAM-DF attains the highest payoff among deployable methods, with gains over a predict-then-threshold baseline across all five ranking sources and two cost regimes. Our approach is state-of-the-art under heterogeneous costs and high cost pressure, with larger gains under weaker rankings. In live execution, CAM-DF exposes the agent to 37\% fewer tools than full access while maintaining comparable task success. The CAM-DF family is a lightweight pre-execution plugin that turns existing tool rankings into lower-cost acquisition decisions without fine-tuning the underlying LLM.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes CAM-DF and CAM-DF-lite, cost-aware stopping methods that determine how many tools an LLM agent should acquire from a ranked list, balancing the trade-off between insufficient and excessive tool access under heterogeneous costs. The approach is trained on offline gaps between stopping and continuing, is Bayes-aligned, and achieves state-of-the-art results across 1,343 tasks in five domains, reducing tool exposure by 37% without compromising task success.
AI.motivation: LLM agents face a fundamental tool-selection dilemma: too few tools leave tasks under-informed, while too many increase cost, context load, and privacy exposure. Existing routers/retrievers rank tools but do not determine how many to select, and no prior work addresses stopping under heterogeneous acquisition costs.
AI.method: The authors formulate tool-selection as cost-aware marginal decision-focused stopping (CAM-DF) over ranked tool prefixes, with a compact interpretable variant CAM-DF-lite. Training uses the offline gap between stopping now vs. the best continuation: the sign of the gap labels the decision, and its magnitude weights each error by the payoff at stake. The objective is proven Bayes-aligned with the stopping target, and score-only rules are shown suboptimal under heterogeneous costs.
AI.result: Evaluated on 1,343 tasks across five tool-use domains. On τ-bench Retail, CAM-DF achieves the highest payoff among deployable methods, outperforming predict-then-threshold baselines across five ranking sources and two cost regimes. State-of-the-art under heterogeneous costs and high cost pressure, with larger gains when rankings are weaker. In live execution, CAM-DF reduces tool exposure by 37% compared to full access while maintaining comparable task success.
AI.conclusion: CAM-DF and its variant provide a lightweight pre-execution plugin that converts existing tool rankings into cost-aware acquisition decisions without fine-tuning the underlying LLM, offering practical gains in efficiency and cost reduction for LLM agent systems.

title: SciFigQual-Bench: A Benchmark for Scientific Figure Quality Assessment with Full-Manuscript Context
comment: † Equal contribution. Affiliations: 1: The University of Hong Kong 2: The University of Sydney 3: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Corresponding authors: Zihan Deng (zhdeng@hku.hk), Chuanzhi Xu (chuanzhi.xu@sydney.edu.au) Project page: https://frankdengai.github.io/SciFigQual-Bench Source code & dataset: https://github.com/FrankDengAI/SciFigQual-Bench
summary: Scientific images are the core elements of presenting experimental conclusions, elaborating system architecture, and supporting comparative arguments in scientific papers. However, existing image quality assessment (IQA) methods are predominantly designed for natural photographs or AI-generated content, which cannot be directly applied to scientific papers. The few existing studies on scholarly charts remain confined to visual-surface comparisons, failing to verify caption alignment, citation relevance, or visual misleadingness. To address this, we propose SciFigQual-Bench, a full-text contextual benchmark that evaluates scientific images across five dimensions (clarity, layout, caption fit, context relevance, and misleading risk). The data covers top computer-science conferences from 2020 to 2025; 6,308 images were independently scored by multiple domain experts in five dimensions and aggregated into gold-standard annotations. Unlike previous scientific figure benchmarks, our dataset binds each image to its caption, citing sentence, and manuscript context. To enable automated evaluation on this benchmark, we designed a staged cross-modal evaluation framework SFQ-Agent to achieve auditable and refined scoring through the collection and fusion of modal evidence. Multiple mainstream large models were evaluated on the test subset eval1200, and SFQ-Agent (F3) equipped with GPT-5.6-Sol achieved the lowest overall average absolute error (0.418) and the highest consistency rate (93.4%), consistently outperforming both direct evaluation and auxiliary (Sidecar) visual language model evaluation schemes.

AI.tldr: SciFigQual-Bench is a full-text contextual benchmark for evaluating scientific images across five dimensions (clarity, layout, caption fit, context relevance, misleading risk), using 6,308 images from top CS conferences (2020-2025) scored by domain experts. The SFQ-Agent framework with GPT-5.6-Sol achieves best performance (0.418 absolute error, 93.4% consistency).
AI.motivation: Existing IQA methods are designed for natural photographs or AI-generated content and cannot be applied to scientific papers. Prior scholarly chart studies only compare visual surfaces without verifying caption alignment, citation relevance, or visual misleadingness.
AI.method: Proposed SciFigQual-Bench with 6,308 images from top CS conferences (2020-2025) scored by multiple domain experts across five dimensions (clarity, layout, caption fit, context relevance, misleading risk). Designed SFQ-Agent, a staged cross-modal evaluation framework for auditable and refined scoring through collection and fusion of modal evidence.
AI.result: SFQ-Agent (F3) with GPT-5.6-Sol achieved lowest average absolute error (0.418) and highest consistency rate (93.4%) on eval1200 test subset, outperforming direct evaluation and auxiliary VLM evaluation schemes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed benchmark and evaluation framework effectively address the gap in scientific image quality assessment by incorporating full-text contextual dimensions beyond visual-surface comparisons.

title: Sky sphere representation in language models
summary:
We analyze whether language models of size ~100B have a representation of the night sky map that is decodable from their residual stream. We find that most of the considered open-source models do have such a representation, and it often even surfaces to the top principal components on prompts that ask questions like ``what is close to this object in the night sky''. In all but one model this representation showed significant scores in LOO testing, containing up to 65-85% of variance ($R^2$-score) and having median angular error down to $12^\circ-21^\circ$. We verify that our representation is not a simple leak from a correlated flat representation. To our knowledge, this representation is the first example of a curved high-dimensional irreducible feature manifold.
  Codes used in the paper are published at https://github.com/l3erdnik/Decodable-sky

AI.tldr: Language models of ~100B parameters encode a decodable representation of the night sky map in their residual stream, with up to 65-85% variance explained and median angular error of 12°-21°, representing the first known curved high-dimensional irreducible feature manifold.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether large language models internally represent structured, curved, high-dimensional feature manifolds (specifically the night sky) beyond simple flat or linear representations.
AI.method: Analyze residual stream activations of ~100B-parameter open-source LMs on prompts about night sky proximity; decode spatial representations via principal component analysis and leave-one-out (LOO) testing; verify representation is not a correlation leak from a flat representation.
AI.result: Most models exhibit decodable night sky representations surfacing in top principal components, achieving R² scores of 65-85% and median angular errors of 12°-21° in LOO testing.
AI.conclusion: Large LMs internally encode curved high-dimensional irreducible feature manifolds, with the night sky map being the first documented example.

title: Step-Attention Refinement of DINOv3 Features for Efficient Anterior Eye Segmentation
summary: Anterior eye segment (AES) segmentation is a key component of both ocular biometrics and emerging clinical image analysis applications. However, heterogeneous acquisition conditions and limited annotations in medical settings hinder the robustness and generalization of existing methods. Foundation models (FMs) such as DINOv3 offer strong transfer capabilities, but efficiently adapting their representations to dense prediction tasks remains challenging. In this study, we investigate robust AES segmentation in clinical settings, and propose a lightweight architecture built upon a distilled DINOv3 ViT-Small backbone. We introduce a step-attention feature refinement module that progressively adapts multi-level transformer representations before convolutional decoding, enabling efficient exploitation of pretrained features with few parameters. We evaluate the proposed approach on a private dataset of 333 clinically acquired AES images spanning eight ophthalmic acquisition protocols and annotated for seven anatomical classes. Compared with convolutional and transformer-based baselines, including DINOv3-based methods, our approach achieves the best overall performance, reaching 85.55\% mIoU when fully fine-tuned. It also demonstrates the strongest robustness to domain shift across four unseen public AES segmentation datasets. These results establish a strong baseline for robust AES segmentation in clinical settings and highlight the importance of decoder design for effectively adapting FMs representations to medical segmentation tasks.

AI.tldr: Proposes a lightweight AES segmentation architecture using a distilled DINOv3 ViT-Small backbone with a step-attention feature refinement module, achieving state-of-the-art performance (85.55% mIoU) and domain robustness on clinical and public datasets.
AI.motivation: Heterogeneous acquisition conditions and limited annotations in medical settings hinder robustness and generalization of existing AES segmentation methods; foundation models offer strong transfer capabilities but efficiently adapting their representations to dense prediction tasks remains challenging.
AI.method: A lightweight architecture built upon a distilled DINOv3 ViT-Small backbone, incorporating a step-attention feature refinement module that progressively adapts multi-level transformer representations before convolutional decoding.
AI.result: Achieves 85.55% mIoU when fully fine-tuned on 333 private AES images (7 classes, 8 protocols); demonstrates strongest robustness to domain shift across four unseen public AES segmentation datasets, outperforming convolutional and transformer-based baselines including other DINOv3-based methods.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a strong baseline for robust AES segmentation in clinical settings and highlights the importance of decoder design for effectively adapting foundation model representations to medical segmentation tasks.

title: Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Coherent Emergency Department Forecasting
comment: Accepted at 11th Workshop on Data Science for Social Good - ECML PKDD 2026
summary: Emergency Departments (EDs) are critical access points in healthcare systems, yet they face persistent pressure from unpredictable patient demand, seasonal surges, and non-urgent visits. Effective ED planning requires forecasts at multiple decision-making levels: hospitals need local demand estimates for staffing and bed management, regions require forecasts to coordinate healthcare units, and national authorities need system-wide projections for capacity planning. However, most existing approaches forecast ED demand independently at a single level, ignoring the hierarchy linking hospitals, regions, and national systems. This can produce incoherent predictions, where hospital-level forecasts do not aggregate consistently to regional or national demand. We propose HierSTT, a hierarchical Transformer-based framework for coherent multi-level ED forecasting. HierSTT jointly predicts hospital, regional, and national level demand in a single end-to-end model. A Temporal Fusion Transformer captures national dynamics, while spatio-temporal Transformer encoder-decoder modules model regional and hospital demand conditioned on higher-level forecasts. A coherence-aware loss penalizes cross-level inconsistencies during training. We further introduce a nationwide Portuguese ED dataset covering 81 hospitals across 5 regional health administrations, with heterogeneous covariates at each level. Experiments show that HierSTT reduces average WAPE by 32\% relative to the best non-hierarchical deep learning baseline and outperforms all classical hierarchical reconciliation methods, while producing near-coherent predictions across levels. Additional resources associated with this work are available at https://github.com/FilipaLino/HierSTT.

AI.tldr: HierSTT is a hierarchical Transformer-based framework for coherent multi-level Emergency Department demand forecasting across hospital, regional, and national levels, achieving 32% WAPE improvement over non-hierarchical baselines on a new nationwide Portuguese ED dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing ED forecasting approaches predict demand independently at a single level (hospital, regional, or national), ignoring the hierarchical structure linking these levels. This leads to incoherent predictions where hospital-level forecasts don't aggregate consistently to higher-level demand, hindering coordinated healthcare planning.
AI.method: HierSTT is an end-to-end hierarchical Transformer with three components: (1) a Temporal Fusion Transformer for national-level dynamics; (2) spatio-temporal Transformer encoder-decoder modules for regional and hospital demand conditioned on higher-level forecasts; (3) a coherence-aware loss function that penalizes cross-level inconsistencies during training. The model jointly predicts all three levels simultaneously.
AI.result: HierSTT reduces average WAPE by 32% relative to the best non-hierarchical deep learning baseline and outperforms all classical hierarchical reconciliation methods on a nationwide Portuguese ED dataset covering 81 hospitals across 5 regional health administrations, while producing near-coherent predictions across levels.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical modeling with coherence constraints significantly improves ED demand forecasting across multiple decision-making levels, enabling consistent and accurate predictions for hospitals, regions, and national health systems simultaneously.

title: FreqForcing: Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Spectral Self-Anchoring
summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models enable real-time streaming video generation. However, errors introduced during self-rollout accumulate over long horizons, manifesting as color drift, motion stagnation, and eventual visual collapse. In this paper, we characterize this phenomenon from a frequency-domain perspective: error accumulation appears as a pronounced energy drift in the low-frequency bands. We further investigate the effectiveness of attention sink in the frequency domain, and find that it improves the video quality by alleviating the spectral energy drift to some extent, but cannot fully resolve it. Motivated by the above analysis, we propose FreqForcing, a training-free framework that addresses error accumulation in long-video generation via Spectral Self-Anchoring (SSA). The proposed SSA leverages the low-frequency components of anchor attention to maintain long-horizon visual stability, while preserving dynamic motion through the high-frequency components of local attention. Our FreqForcing extends Self-Forcing pretrained on 5s clips to two-minute generation, achieving 24x extrapolation. Extensive experiments show that FreqForcing outperforms existing training-free methods quantitatively and qualitatively while remaining competitive with representative training-based approaches.

AI.tldr: FreqForcing is a training-free framework that uses Spectral Self-Anchoring (SSA) to fix error accumulation in autoregressive video diffusion models for long-video generation, achieving 24x extrapolation (from 5s to 2 minutes) by stabilizing low-frequency spectral energy drift via anchor attention while preserving motion through high-frequency local attention.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive video diffusion models suffer from error accumulation during long-horizon self-rollout, causing color drift, motion stagnation, and visual collapse. The authors characterize this as low-frequency spectral energy drift and find that attention sink only partially alleviates the issue.
AI.method: Proposes FreqForcing with Spectral Self-Anchoring (SSA): uses low-frequency components of anchor attention to maintain visual stability and high-frequency components of local attention to preserve dynamic motion. It is training-free and extends Self-Forcing pretrained on 5s clips.
AI.result: Achieves 24x extrapolation (5s to 2 minutes generation). Outperforms existing training-free methods both quantitatively and qualitatively, and remains competitive with training-based approaches.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-domain analysis reveals that error accumulation corresponds to low-frequency spectral energy drift. FreqForcing effectively resolves this drift via SSA without additional training, enabling stable long-video generation.

title: Voronoi Histograms for Adaptive Vectorization of Expected Persistence Diagrams
summary: Persistence Diagram (PD) is known to capture point cloud topology effectively, but its computation has high time complexity. Expected Persistence Diagram (EPD) has been developed to reduce the time cost by studying the topology of multiple subsets of a point cloud and it serves as a distribution of topological features. Existing EPD vectorizations often rely on predefined point transformations, such as Gaussian or landscape functions. We study an alternative discretization based on Voronoi histograms, which trades smooth functional approximation for adaptive partition-based counting. We propose to use Voronoi Diagram-based histogram as the vectorization of EPD, without imposing an explicit smooth point transformation model. Under stated separation and normalization conditions, we establish stability bounds and characterize when the histogram representation preserves Wasserstein-scale variation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed representation on real-world datasets which have significant topological features for classification and dimensionality reduction tasks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using Voronoi Diagram-based histograms as a vectorization method for Expected Persistence Diagrams (EPD), offering a computationally efficient alternative to traditional smooth transformation-based approaches while providing stability guarantees and demonstrating effectiveness on real-world classification and dimensionality reduction tasks.
AI.motivation: Persistence Diagram (PD) computation has high time complexity. Expected Persistence Diagram (EPD) reduces cost by studying topology of multiple subsets, but existing EPD vectorizations rely on predefined smooth point transformations (e.g., Gaussian or landscape functions), which may be suboptimal.
AI.method: The authors propose using Voronoi Diagram-based histograms as the vectorization of EPD, replacing explicit smooth point transformation models with adaptive partition-based counting. They establish stability bounds under separation and normalization conditions and characterize when the histogram representation preserves Wasserstein-scale variation.
AI.result: The proposed Voronoi histogram representation demonstrates effectiveness on real-world datasets with significant topological features for classification and dimensionality reduction tasks.
AI.conclusion: Voronoi histogram-based vectorization of EPD is a viable alternative to smooth functional approaches, trading smooth approximation for adaptive partition-based counting with provable stability guarantees.

title: Veritas++: Value-aware On-Policy Distillation for Perception-Enhanced AIGI Detection
summary: The growing capability of image generation models has made synthetic images a routine presence in open media, making robust and generalizable AI-Generated Image (AIGI) detection increasingly essential. While multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) offer a transparent alternative to black-box binary scoring, we observe that current MLLM-based detectors still exhibit notable perception bottlenecks in capturing fine-grained anomalies. They primarily focus on how visual evidence is organized and synthesized, leaving the intrinsic perception less optimized. To mitigate this gap, we present Veritas++, a perception-enhanced reasoning framework that establishes reliable perception as the foundation of authenticity reasoning. Rather than directly optimizing the model's explanatory ability, we ground AIGI detection on three basic perception abilities, i.e., capturing fine-grained visual details, semantic anomalies and pixel-level differences. Building on this insight, we introduce Perception-oriented Learning (PoRL), which replaces open-ended description supervision with verifiable rewards to explicitly strengthen these capacities. To further integrate enhanced perception with reasoning, we introduce Value-aware On-Policy Distillation (VaOPD), an adaptive distillation mechanism that prioritizes high-value distillation signals over uniform supervision, internalizing perception-aware reasoning through a privileged self-teacher. Extensive experiments across standard, in-the-wild and emerging benchmarks demonstrate that Veritas++ achieves promising generalization. The perception learning effectively bridges the perception gap and yields seamless gains on detection, while VaOPD further enables efficient capability evolvement without sacrificing existing performance. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/EricTan7/VeritasPP.

AI.tldr: Veritas++ is a perception-enhanced reasoning framework for AI-generated image detection that replaces open-ended description supervision with verifiable rewards (PoRL) and uses Value-aware On-Policy Distillation (VaOPD) to improve fine-grained anomaly perception in MLLMs, achieving promising generalization across benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current MLLM-based AIGI detectors exhibit perception bottlenecks in capturing fine-grained anomalies; they focus on how visual evidence is organized and synthesized while leaving intrinsic perception less optimized. The goal is to establish reliable perception as the foundation of authenticity reasoning.
AI.method: 1) Grounds AIGI detection on three basic perception abilities: fine-grained visual details, semantic anomalies, and pixel-level differences. 2) Perception-oriented Learning (PoRL): replaces open-ended description supervision with verifiable rewards to explicitly strengthen perception capacities. 3) Value-aware On-Policy Distillation (VaOPD): adaptive distillation mechanism that prioritizes high-value distillation signals via a privileged self-teacher.
AI.result: Veritas++ achieves promising generalization across standard, in-the-wild, and emerging benchmarks. Perception learning bridges the perception gap and yields seamless detection gains; VaOPD enables efficient capability evolvement without sacrificing existing performance.
AI.conclusion: The perception-enhanced reasoning framework effectively addresses the perception gap in MLLM-based AIGI detection, providing a transparent alternative to black-box binary scoring while achieving robust generalization.

title: Minimal Markovization via Stable Quotients in Holonomy-Cover Decision Processes
summary: An agent acting under partial observability must retain a recursively updateable statistic of history that restores the Markov property, but the smallest such statistic is generally unknown. We characterize this minimal Markov sufficient statistic for holonomy-cover decision processes, a structured POMDP class in which the visible dynamics are Markov and every realized visible transition applies a fixed permutation to a hidden mode. In particular, we construct the stable quotient, the coarsest observation-wise abstraction preserving one-step rewards and quotient successors, and prove that the pair of the current observation and stable class forms an exact finite Markov state. When the current class is correctly initialized, exact class tracking requires exactly the minimal memory symbols, in the sense that under reachability and pairwise decision separation at a maximizing observation, no arbitrary finite-memory controller can use fewer. Under resettable diagnostics, nearest-prototype class inference has exponentially decaying error, and a calibrate-then-restart reduction transfers finite-MDP guarantees to the recovered state. The results enable \emph{Holonomy Memory Reinforcement Learning}. It represents memory by the current stable class, updates it through ordered edge transports, identifies local class coordinates when diagnostics are available, and applies a standard finite-MDP RL backbone after synchronization. Experiments recover an exact compression from raw states to quotient states and achieve perfect paired-order accuracy with three decision-time memory states, matching the quotient oracle and outperforming the non-oracle baselines.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes the minimal Markov sufficient statistic (stable quotient) for holonomy-cover decision processes, a structured POMDP class, proving it forms an exact finite Markov state. The authors construct a stable quotient abstraction, show its memory minimality under reachability and decision separation, and develop Holonomy Memory Reinforcement Learning (HMRL) with exponentially decaying inference error and finite-MDP guarantees.
AI.motivation: In partially observable environments, agents need a recursively updateable statistic of history to restore the Markov property, but the minimal such statistic is generally unknown. This paper aims to characterize this minimal Markov sufficient statistic for a specific structured POMDP class (holonomy-cover decision processes) to enable efficient reinforcement learning.
AI.method: The authors characterize holonomy-cover decision processes where visible dynamics are Markov and each visible transition applies a fixed permutation to a hidden mode. They construct the stable quotient (coarsest observation-wise abstraction preserving rewards and quotient successors), prove its Markov property and minimality, and develop HMRL which tracks stable classes through ordered edge transports, identifies local class coordinates via resettable diagnostics, and applies finite-MDP RL after synchronization.
AI.result: Experiments recover exact compression from raw states to quotient states, achieve perfect paired-order accuracy with three decision-time memory states matching the quotient oracle, and outperform non-oracle baselines. The stable quotient provides exponentially decaying inference error under resettable diagnostics.
AI.conclusion: The stable quotient is the exact minimal Markov sufficient statistic for holonomy-cover decision processes, enabling Holonomy Memory RL to transfer finite-MDP guarantees to partially observable settings through calibration and synchronization.

title: Towards Grounded GI Endoscopy VQA via Multi-Task Learning on Small VLMs
comment: Accepted at EMA4MICCAI 2026 (Workshop on Efficient Medical AI, MICCAI 2026)
summary: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopic image analysis has shifted from single-label classification toward visual question answering (VQA), where a model must answer free-form clinical questions about an image. While recent vision-language models (VLMs) achieve promising answer accuracy on this task, clinical adoption also requires the model's internal representations to reflect the visual evidence behind its answers. We propose a simple multi-task fine-tuning recipe that constructs auxiliary grounding and description tasks from an existing VQA dataset with minimal additional annotation: expert-annotated polyp masks are reused directly, while a GI-domain pretrained classifier with Grad-CAM localization provides weak supervision for finding categories that lack ground-truth masks. Three small VLM backbones are fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation under matched VQA-only and multi-task recipes on Kvasir-VQA-x1, and we show consistent accuracy gains together with improved implicit alignment between answer tokens and the relevant image region, evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution data.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a multi-task fine-tuning recipe for GI endoscopic VQA that adds auxiliary grounding and description tasks using minimal extra annotation, improving both answer accuracy and implicit visual grounding in small VLMs.
AI.motivation: Clinical adoption of VQA for GI endoscopy requires not just answer accuracy but also interpretability—models must reflect the visual evidence behind their answers, which current VLMs lack.
AI.method: A multi-task fine-tuning approach that constructs auxiliary grounding (polyp mask supervision) and description (Grad-CAM weak supervision from a GI-domain classifier) tasks from an existing VQA dataset. Three small VLMs are fine-tuned with LoRA under matched VQA-only and multi-task recipes on Kvasir-VQA-x1.
AI.result: Consistent accuracy gains on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution data, plus improved implicit alignment between answer tokens and relevant image regions.
AI.conclusion: Multi-task fine-tuning with minimal extra annotation can simultaneously boost VQA performance and enhance model interpretability via better visual grounding in GI endoscopic image analysis.

title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
summary: High-stakes decision systems in credit scoring, fraud detection, healthcare, and industrial safety require reliable uncertainty quantification under severe class imbalance and asymmetric error costs. Standard marginal conformal prediction (CP) provides valid overall coverage guarantees; however, we show that it severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes, with minority-class coverage dropping to as low as 0.5% on certain datasets. To characterize and address this limitation, we conduct a comprehensive benchmark comparing marginal CP, class-conditional (Mondrian) CP, and cost-controlled abstention mechanisms across 15 real-world imbalanced tabular datasets, 7 classification models, 3 probability calibration techniques, and 10 random seeds, resulting in 3,150 experimental runs. Our results show that Mondrian CP restores valid minority-class coverage, achieving an average minority-coverage improvement of 61.7 percentage points over marginal CP (p < 1e-80). Furthermore, combining Mondrian CP with cost-controlled abstention significantly reduces expected decision cost compared with standard decision boundaries, confidence-based rejectors, and risk-controlled rejectors under realistic human review budgets. We further quantify dataset-specific break-even thresholds at which deferring ambiguous instances to human experts becomes cost-effective. These findings provide practical guidance for deploying distribution-free, cost-aware uncertainty quantification in high-stakes decision support systems.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks conformal prediction methods under class imbalance, showing that marginal CP severely under-covers minority classes (as low as 0.5%), while Mondrian CP restores valid coverage (+61.7 pp on average). Combining Mondrian CP with cost-controlled abstention reduces expected decision cost, with practical break-even thresholds for human review deferral identified across 3,150 experimental runs.
AI.motivation: High-stakes decision systems (credit scoring, fraud detection, healthcare, industrial safety) require reliable uncertainty quantification under severe class imbalance and asymmetric error costs, but standard marginal conformal prediction fails to provide adequate coverage for rare minority classes.
AI.method: Comprehensive benchmark comparing marginal CP, class-conditional (Mondrian) CP, and cost-controlled abstention mechanisms across 15 real-world imbalanced tabular datasets, 7 classification models, 3 calibration techniques, and 10 random seeds (3,150 total experimental runs).
AI.result: Mondrian CP achieves average minority-coverage improvement of 61.7 percentage points over marginal CP (p < 1e-80). Combining Mondrian CP with cost-controlled abstention significantly reduces expected decision cost compared to standard decision boundaries, confidence-based rejectors, and risk-controlled rejectors under realistic human review budgets.
AI.conclusion: Provides practical guidance for deploying distribution-free, cost-aware uncertainty quantification in high-stakes decision support systems, including dataset-specific break-even thresholds for cost-effective deferral to human experts.

title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI
summary: Accurate 3D reconstruction from satellite imagery typically relies on near-simultaneous stereo pairs, limiting its applicability to diachronic settings where multi-date images exhibit varying seasonal and illumination conditions. Training dense stereo matching models robust to appearance changes is a long-standing challenge, as aligned multi-date imagery and ground-truth geometry are costly to obtain at scale. We propose SeasonStereo, a scalable framework that addresses disparity estimation from diachronic satellite images by training on synthetic image pairs with controlled seasonal appearance variation, while leveraging zero-shot geometric priors from foundation models. SeasonStereo matches the accuracy of state-of-the-art LiDAR-supervised models, while producing sharper geometric details without requiring aligned real multi-date training products or LiDAR-derived labels. As a result, SeasonStereo offers a practical path toward large-scale 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous satellite images with reduced supervision cost.

AI.tldr: SeasonStereo enables accurate 3D reconstruction from diachronic satellite images (different dates, seasons, illumination) by training on synthetic image pairs with controlled seasonal variation and using zero-shot geometric priors from foundation models, matching LiDAR-supervised models without needing real multi-date training data or LiDAR labels.
AI.motivation: Traditional satellite 3D reconstruction requires near-simultaneous stereo pairs, failing in diachronic settings where images have varying seasonal and illumination conditions. Dense stereo matching robust to appearance changes is challenging because aligned multi-date imagery with ground-truth geometry is costly to obtain at scale.
AI.method: SeasonStereo trains on synthetic image pairs with controlled seasonal appearance variation, and leverages zero-shot geometric priors from foundation models to guide disparity estimation.
AI.result: Matches the accuracy of state-of-the-art LiDAR-supervised models while producing sharper geometric details, without requiring aligned real multi-date training data or LiDAR-derived labels.
AI.conclusion: Offers a practical, scalable path toward large-scale 3D reconstruction from heterogeneous satellite images with reduced supervision cost.

title: Skillful forecasting of offshore winds from satellite scatterometer constellations
summary: Accurate intraday forecasts of offshore wind are becoming increasingly important for power system operation and the integration of growing shares of offshore wind energy. Operational forecasts rely predominantly on numerical weather prediction (NWP), which is not optimized for lead times of minutes to hours, where initial-condition accuracy dominates forecast skill. Although satellite scatterometer observations are routinely assimilated into NWP, they have not previously been used directly for forecasting. Here we present WindCastNet, the first satellite-based nowcasting framework for offshore wind speed and direction, introducing a new paradigm for intraday forecasting that learns from spatiotemporally irregular satellite observations. WindCastNet predicts offshore wind fields from observations acquired by satellite scatterometer constellations. WindCastNet employs a partial convolutional long short-term memory network that exploits microwave radar observations from the European, Chinese, and Indian scatterometers despite their irregular spatial coverage, asynchronous sampling, and variable revisit times. Spatial observation masks and inter-observation intervals are encoded, while a continuous temporal representation enables forecasts at arbitrary lead times. Evaluated over the North Sea, WindCastNet reduces the root-mean-square error by 23% and 7% relative to the HARMONIE MEPS model at lead times of 1 and 2 h, respectively, and outperforms persistence by 9-15% during the first three forecast hours. Forecast skill decreases under strong-wind conditions and spatially non-uniform flow. These results demonstrate that satellite scatterometer constellations can provide an independent and competitive source of short-term offshore wind forecasts, opening new opportunities for renewable energy forecasting but also broader marine weather applications, including tropical cyclone nowcasting.

AI.tldr: WindCastNet is the first satellite-based nowcasting framework for offshore wind speed and direction, using a partial convolutional LSTM network with scatterometer data from multiple satellite constellations. It outperforms the HARMONIE MEPS NWP model by 23% and 7% RMSE reduction at 1- and 2-hour lead times, respectively, over the North Sea.
AI.motivation: Intraday offshore wind forecasts are critical for power system operation, but existing NWP methods are not optimized for short lead times (minutes to hours) where initial-condition accuracy matters most. Satellite scatterometer data, though routinely assimilated into NWP, had never been used directly for forecasting before.
AI.method: WindCastNet employs a partial convolutional LSTM network that processes irregularly sampled scatterometer observations from European, Chinese, and Indian satellite constellations. It encodes spatial observation masks and inter-observation intervals, uses a continuous temporal representation for arbitrary lead-time forecasts, and handles asynchronous sampling and variable revisit times.
AI.result: Over the North Sea, WindCastNet reduces RMSE by 23% (1h) and 7% (2h) versus HARMONIE MEPS, outperforms persistence by 9-15% in the first three forecast hours. Performance degrades under strong-wind conditions and spatially non-uniform flow.
AI.conclusion: Satellite scatterometer constellations can serve as an independent, competitive source for short-term offshore wind forecasting, opening opportunities for renewable energy forecasting and broader marine weather applications like tropical cyclone nowcasting.

title: Explainable and Resource-Efficient Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Decision-Critical Applications
summary: As Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in decision-critical pipelines such as robotics, embodied AI, and safety monitoring, the opacity of their spatial judgments limits operator trust and auditability. MLLMs demonstrate strong reasoning but often struggle with fine-grained spatial understanding and object hallucination. Prior work, ByDeWay, introduced Layered-Depth-Based Prompting (LDP), a training-free framework that mitigates hallucinations by structuring prompts using monocular depth estimation. However, coarse depth layering falls short in resolving object-to-object spatial relationships within the same geometric plane, such as projective ("left of", "above") and topological ("inside", "touching") relations. We propose ByDeWay-V2, which integrates explicit spatial relational context alongside depth cues, expressed as human-readable predicates that serve as auditable evidence for downstream decision support. Using an open-vocabulary object detector (YOLO-World-L), our framework computes pairwise geometric relations between detected objects and injects them as structured spatial predicates into the MLLM prompt, bridging 3D scene depth and 2D spatial semantics without any training. We evaluate ByDeWay-V2 on the Visual Spatial Reasoning (VSR) and BLINK benchmarks across multiple MLLMs, with hallucination grounding assessed via POPE. On the BLINK spatial subset, ByDeWay-V2 achieves a 46 percent relative F1 improvement over LDP for Qwen2.5-VL, and recovers BLIP-Base's spatial reasoning on VSR from near-random performance to a competitive F1 of 0.53. Our lightest configuration operates under a strict 40-token context budget on CPU, showing the framework's suitability for resource-constrained, real-time decision-support settings.

AI.tldr: ByDeWay-V2 enhances MLLM spatial reasoning by injecting explicit pairwise geometric relations (projective and topological) into prompts using an open-vocabulary detector, achieving significant F1 improvements on VSR and BLINK benchmarks without training, even under tight computational budgets.
AI.motivation: MLLMs deployed in decision-critical pipelines (robotics, embodied AI, safety monitoring) suffer from opaque spatial judgments, fine-grained spatial understanding limitations, and object hallucination. Prior work (ByDeWay/LDP) using coarse depth layering fails to resolve object-to-object spatial relationships within the same geometric plane, such as projective and topological relations.
AI.method: ByDeWay-V2 integrates explicit spatial relational context by using YOLO-World-L (open-vocabulary object detector) to compute pairwise geometric relations between detected objects, then injects these as structured spatial predicates (human-readable) into MLLM prompts. This bridges 3D scene depth and 2D spatial semantics without any training.
AI.result: On BLINK spatial subset, ByDeWay-V2 achieves 46% relative F1 improvement over LDP for Qwen2.5-VL. Recovers BLIP-Base's VSR spatial reasoning from near-random to F1 of 0.53. Lightest configuration operates under 40-token context budget on CPU, suitable for resource-constrained real-time settings.
AI.conclusion: ByDeWay-V2 provides auditable, training-free spatial reasoning enhancement for MLLMs, effectively bridging depth and semantics, with demonstrated gains on multiple benchmarks and feasibility for edge deployment.

title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems
summary: Solving a continuous algebraic constraint system requires two decisions: which values satisfy the constraints, and which structural augmentation renders an unsolvable system solvable. Classical solvers answer the first well and the second only by enumeration. On that discrete decision, a candidate-conditioned repair ranker choosing among K augmentations reaches the exhaustive-search ceiling at a fraction of the calls, outperforming random (0.997 vs 0.236 balanced nonlinear menu accuracy; p < 10^-70; 0.982 +/- 0.006 across seeds) and beating a budget-matched per-candidate probe on accuracy and cost. MARC turns such a system into a factor graph, over which a graph-neural diffusion denoiser proposes assignments, descent on an exact computer-algebra energy polishes them, and an exact symbolic checker certifies solutions. Evaluations of diffusion-based proposals rarely include one control: random multi-start under the same refinement budget. Applied to our system, it sharply curtails what the learned proposal contributes on the value decision. Does it beat random multi-start at choosing satisfying assignments? Only narrowly, in a predictable regime. Across trapped low-dimensional families it ties with random restart, but dominates in high dimension, where random search fails. Once variables couple, the advantage is gone. Since all methods share one polish and one checker, best-of-K random multi-start succeeds with probability exactly 1 - (1 - q(n))^K, where q(n) is single-start reachability; one measured constant, with no free parameters, reproduces the entire curve (mean absolute error 0.012). The favorable regime is not specific to our synthetic families: across eight real-world systems in robotics, positioning, optimization, and algebra, classical multi-start solved all eight, none in the learning-favorable regime. We map the regimes in which learned proposals improve solvers.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces MARC, a method that solves continuous algebraic constraint systems by using a graph-neural diffusion denoiser for value assignments and a repair ranker for structural augmentation. The learned proposal only narrowly beats random multi-start in high-dimensional regimes, and across eight real-world systems, classical multi-start solved all, none in the learning-favorable regime.
AI.motivation: Solving continuous algebraic constraint systems requires both finding satisfying values and deciding structural augmentations when systems are unsolvable. Classical solvers handle the first well but only enumerate the second. The authors aim to improve both decisions with learned components while rigorously evaluating whether learning actually adds value over simpler baselines like random multi-start.
AI.method: MARC transforms the constraint system into a factor graph, applies graph-neural diffusion denoising to propose assignments, refines them via descent on exact computer-algebra energy, and certifies solutions with symbolic checking. For structural augmentation, a candidate-conditioned repair ranker selects among K augmentations. The learned proposal is compared against random multi-start with the same refinement budget, and a best-of-K random multi-start model with no free parameters predicts performance accurately.
AI.result: The repair ranker achieves 0.997 vs 0.236 balanced accuracy (p < 10^-70), beating enumeration. The learned proposal for value decisions only narrowly beats random multi-start in high-dimensional regimes; in low-dimensional families it ties, and when variables couple, the advantage disappears. Across eight real-world systems, classical multi-start solved all, none in the learning-favorable regime. The best-of-K random multi-start model reproduces the entire curve with MAE 0.012.
AI.conclusion: The paper maps the regimes where learned proposals improve solvers and where they do not. Learning provides value for structural augmentation decisions but offers only limited advantage for value assignments, primarily in high-dimensional settings. Random multi-start with sufficient budget is surprisingly competitive, and the simple analytical model accurately predicts its behavior.

title: Anatomy Contextualized Adaption of CT Foundation Models
comment: Accepted to the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026 MedFM-Bench Workshop
summary: CT vision-language foundation models have demonstrated promising performance across downstream tasks, but are typically trained with whole-volume representations that dilute fine-grained anatomical signals. Fine-grained vision-language pre-training addresses this by aligning anatomy-level visual features with anatomy-specific text, but in doing so discards the global context that whole-volume models provide. Furthermore, existing fine-grained approaches train from scratch, making them computationally expensive. We introduce Anatomy Contextualized Adaptation (ACA), a lightweight framework that adapts frozen CT foundation model representations for anatomy-level vision-language alignment while enhancing global contextualization. ACA uses TotalSegmentator to decompose CT volumes into anatomy-level embeddings, which are refined via a transformer that captures cross-anatomy relationships, and aligned to both per-anatomy and scan-level text extracted from radiology reports. Evaluated on Merlin and CT-RATE, ACA consistently outperforms both the frozen foundation model baselines and existing fine-grained methods in zero-shot finding classification, while requiring less than one hour of training once embeddings are cached. The attention weights learned by ACA's inter-anatomy transformer additionally indicate plausible cross-anatomy context routing. Altogether, these results support ACA as a lightweight approach for adapting CT foundation models to anatomically grounded vision-language alignment while preserving and enhancing global anatomical context.

AI.tldr: ACA is a lightweight framework that adapts frozen CT foundation models for anatomy-level vision-language alignment while preserving global context, achieving superior zero-shot classification with under one hour of training.
AI.motivation: Existing CT vision-language models either use whole-volume representations (diluting fine-grained signals) or fine-grained anatomy-level approaches (discarding global context and requiring expensive training from scratch). ACA aims to combine the strengths of both paradigms efficiently.
AI.method: ACA uses TotalSegmentator to decompose CT volumes into anatomy-level embeddings, processes them through a transformer for inter-anatomy relationships, and aligns them to per-anatomy and scan-level text from radiology reports, while keeping the foundation model frozen.
AI.result: ACA consistently outperforms frozen foundation model baselines and existing fine-grained methods in zero-shot finding classification on Merlin and CT-RATE datasets, with less than one hour of training after embedding caching.
AI.conclusion: ACA provides a lightweight approach for adapting CT foundation models to anatomically grounded vision-language alignment while preserving and enhancing global anatomical context, with interpretable attention weights indicating plausible cross-anatomy context routing.

title: Inverse Learning of Latent Risk-Neutral Densities from Irregular Option Quotes
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 7th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF 2026)
summary: Accurate option prices do not imply accurate recovery of the latent risk-neutral density. We study this distinction with two complementary benchmarks. A controlled benchmark exposes simulator-truth densities for latent evaluation, while a chronological NIFTY benchmark tests only held-out market prices. A two-component lognormal mixture has the lowest aggregate price, $L^1$, Wasserstein, and fixed-tail errors on the synthetic benchmark. Learned operators retain narrower strengths: DeepONet reduces 1% quantile and variance error by 39.0% and 34.6% relative to the mixture, and a quote transformer reduces $L^1$ by 16.4% on the structurally misspecified Merton family. A numerical conditioning analysis explains why these rankings can differ: after enforcing mass and forward constraints, 95 of 126 pricing directions are numerically null, and two densities separated by $L^1 = 0.061$ produce identical prices on the covered strikes. On 524 held-out NIFTY calls, validation-selected test-time adaptation reduces DeepONet RMSE by 28.3%, but per-expiry mixture and SVI fits remain much more accurate. The evidence supports target-dependent inductive bias, not a universal winner.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that accurate option prices do not guarantee accurate recovery of risk-neutral densities, using synthetic and real benchmarks. A lognormal mixture performs best overall, but learned methods excel in specific aspects (e.g., DeepONet for quantile/variance errors). Numerical conditioning reveals many pricing directions are null, and no single method universally dominates.
